notes: The phone app: Menu, What's new has a new Check for updates - it looks for a newer version there and then, and tells you what it found. The app also looks by itself more often: when you open it and whenever you come back to it, up to once an hour (it was once every 6 hours, and only as it opened).

The course designer is in the web version: press Course designer in the Course tab (or New course... in the course picker) to make a course in a few clicks or from a scorecard, change any hole, and play it - on a computer, a tablet or a phone. The courses you make are kept in that browser, and Share... gives one a code to send to your PC, the phone app or a friend. Real courses from the map are still made on the PC.
Friends' courses on the phone app and the web version are now kept where there's far more room, so even a big course on hills is kept.

Keep the courses you make in your own Google Drive, if you like: Google Drive... in the Course tab (and under Your courses in the designer) turns it on - it's off unless you do. A course made or changed on one PC or browser is then on every other one you've turned it on in; one deleted goes to Google Drive's bin. On the PC it uses the Google sign-in from My stats; the web version asks Google when you turn it on.

The phone app has the course designer too: Course designer on Home, in the Course tab, or New course... in the course picker. Make a course in a few taps or from a scorecard, change any hole by touch, play it, and Share... it by a code. The courses you make are kept on the phone.
In the designer on a phone's screen, Your courses now folds under its heading, so the course you're making is the first thing you see.

On a phone you can drive the cart between holes: tap Drive it, then the arrows under your thumb are its speed and its steering. Held upright, the cart's bar now goes neatly across the picture instead of wrapping over the shot's numbers, and the scorecard on the cart's screen is big enough to read.

The cart between holes waits for you now instead of setting off: choose Auto drive and it takes itself to the next tee, or Drive it and take the wheel - and swap between the two whenever you like (handed back, it finds its way from wherever you've got to). While you drive, an arrow on the bar points the way to the next tee and says how far it is. Next hole is there the whole time.
A round's first hole is ready sooner: the game draws it in the background while you're on the range, so starting a round no longer waits for it (it could take five seconds). On the PC.

Lighter on the top graphics setting: the beech, birch, hawthorn, poplar and Scots pine rebuilt earlier this week had become heavier to draw close up, where most trees are drawn on that setting. They're back to what they were, and look the same.

You can drive the cart yourself between holes: choose Watch the drive, press ↑ and the cart is yours - ↑ and ↓ for faster, slower and reverse, ← and → to steer - anywhere round the hole, over the grass and along the paths. Water, bunkers, trees and signs stop it, and Next hole plays on from wherever you've got to. First go at it: the keyboard, or a controller's D-pad.

The horse chestnut's flower candles are smaller and slimmer and take the light of the side of the tree they're on, instead of standing out as flat cream shapes; its leaves are a touch lighter, so its shaded side isn't black.
The Scots pine has a wider, flatter, lopsided head instead of a tidy cone, and the beech's trunk forks into boughs under its crown, as the ordinary broadleaf's does.

Faster with the picture's centre moved: the game was being drawn a third wider than the screen all the time the command centre's video monitor box was showing - only a recording needs that - which cost about ten frames a second on the range. It's drawn wide only while recording or laying out the video now.

The solid shapes under a tree's leaves no longer show as dark balls: they're lit as part of the whole tree and are nearer the leaves' own colour - most on the beech, the holly and the willow's top. The beech is also lighter to draw.
The speed test's links hole no longer has dunes standing through the other holes' fairways as it flies over them.

Every kind of tree is more its own: hollies have spiny, glossy leaves and bunches of red berries; hawthorns have small lobed leaves, are white with blossom in spring and carry red haws from summer; beeches have flat sprays of pointed leaves; and spruces, Scots pines and cedars each have needles of their own instead of sharing the pine's.

Broadleaved trees look fuller and deeper: the ends of their shoots stand out from the crown, and what shows between the leaves is more leaves in shade, not a plain green shape. They also take less to draw than before. On Medium graphics and up.

Horse chestnuts look like horse chestnuts: big hand-shaped leaves of five to seven leaflets in a deep green, and candles of white flowers standing over the crown - now and then pink - on most of them, though not in autumn. On High and Ultra the ends of its shoots stand out from the crown as rosettes of leaves, drooping at their tips, so it has depth close to. On Medium graphics and up; the first of the trees being made more their own.

The phone app signs in with Google: on the sign-in card press Continue with Google, sign in on the page that opens in your phone's browser, and you're brought back into the game as you. Email and password work as before.
The phone app: the Open in the A² Golf app button on the page for linking a phone to your PC now opens the app, with the code typed in.

Lighter on the graphics card: trees a pitch shot or more away are drawn with simpler trunks (they look the same from there), and the picture's effects only take the card's memory when they're switched on - on High at 4K that's about 160 MB less. Nothing should look different.

On a 1440p or 4K screen the club, the numbers and the messages over the picture keep their size against the screen (they used to stop growing, so on a 4K projector they were half as big as they should be), and the menu, the Online panel and the cards that ask something are drawn larger too rather than as a small box in the middle. Nothing changes at 1080p.

Tidier menus and screens: on a small laptop screen the menu's last page (Help) is no longer half hidden; the menu's drop-down lists line up down the page; in bay view the player, club, result and connection sit on one line; in the side panel the game buttons (Practice, Distance challenge, Golf pong and the like) are neat single-line pills and a setting's name stays on one line beside its list; and the shot data window says what each box is waiting for before the first shot instead of showing an empty badge and blank boxes.
New in Menu, Screens (on a screen bigger than 1080p): Bigger top bar and side panel - draws them larger on a 1440p or 4K screen, as the menu is there. Off unless you turn it on.
On trial: the long grass right round you is drawn a third lighter. It should look the same - Menu, Graphics, Lighter long grass round you switches it off and on where you stand, to compare.

More of the trees lining a hole are drawn at their best - their branches and finer leaves - on High graphics: out to 140 m ahead of you, where it was 110. The game no longer spends that detail on trees behind where you're standing, which you never see, and gives it to the ones ahead.

Tree trunks stand in the shade of their own crowns: darker and cooler up into the leaves, instead of evenly lit orange posts - a wood down the side of a hole reads as shaded. A birch's white bark stays pale.

Small things on the trees, closer to the real thing: the tips of the shoots are this year's lighter, yellower green; there's moss up one side of a trunk's foot; crowns are a little deeper underneath and vary more from bough to bough; and the beech's leaves no longer show flat dark shapes between them.

Five kinds of tree rebuilt after a hard look at each: the beech is a full, leafy tree with a pale grey trunk instead of dark balls on a post; the ordinary broadleaf's trunk forks into boughs that carry its crown, so it's no longer a ball on a stick; the hawthorn is one dense dome; the birch has enough leaves to be a tree; the poplar is fuller. Medium graphics and up.

Behind the scenes: the game keeps in memory only the kinds of tree in use - those of the range, the practice greens and the course you're playing - and lets go of tree parts it never draws: about 11 MB less on High and Ultra, and up to 20 MB more on a course with few kinds of tree. Nothing should look or play differently.

Share a course you've made with friends: pick it in the Course tab and press Share... for its code, a link and a QR code. They press Friend's course... - on their PC, the phone app or the web version - type the code or paste the link, and it's theirs to play, their rounds and bests on it their own. The course picker lists them under From: Friends' courses.

A season by post can go round your own courses and friends' too (Courses: Those and my other courses when you make it): each is shared as the season's made, and anyone who hasn't got it has it fetched when they play that event.

Five new kinds of tree: beeches (now and then a deep purple copper beech), horse chestnuts, great flat-layered cedars of Lebanon, dark glossy hollies and small twisted hawthorns - near and far, in the woods and along the hedges.

Each hole now grows a few kinds of tree rather than a bit of everything, in stands - a patch of beeches beside a patch of oaks, a group of hollies - with most kinds carrying on into the next hole and the odd new one coming in along the round. Holes you've already played keep their trees until you grow them afresh in the hole editor.

Some holes have a signature tree: a big lone oak, cedar, beech or horse chestnut at the corner of the landing area or beside the approach. The hole editor shows it ringed in gold and can take it away or put it back.

The hole editor keeps planting natural: the kinds already on the hole are listed first, a hole takes at most five kinds, and it won't plant a third kind in among two that already mix - it says why and what would fit instead.

Safer online and at home: a game found on your home network, another player's name or a host's course can no longer slip anything onto your screen but plain text - a name with odd characters in it just shows as typed.

In the Windows app, links to other websites open in your browser as before, but nothing else (a file or another program) is opened from a link; and a program to start with A² Golf can only be added with its Browse button.
Behind the scenes: the game's own server on your PC now only answers A² Golf's own pages, and a few more checks on what it's sent. Nothing should play differently.
Postal ladder: Watch the round shows again after the reveal - their shots hole by hole beside yours.

On the course: a gimme is never given on your tenth stroke, so a tenth shot scores ten whether it finished close or not; a mulligan after a hole's scorecard came up takes the card down; and pressing N twice no longer starts two rounds.
Trying one hole from the course designer no longer saves it as a round of the course.
In an online, ladder or season round, Start round and adding or removing players are refused with a word why (they'd have thrown the round away), and renaming a player renames the right one.
A ladder result that couldn't be sent (no connection) is kept and sent again the next time you open the ladder or press Refresh, instead of being lost.
Typing a name or a code in the online and ladder panels is no longer wiped by the panel redrawing itself.
A mouse or controller chip still rolling when a real shot comes in is now kept as the made-up swing it was, and the real shot as real (it could get them the wrong way round).
If a shot can't be saved to your stats, it's tried once more and then you're told, and Delete no longer takes out the shot before it by mistake.
A session recording that can't be saved carries on in a new file rather than quietly filling memory.
A player whose very first stats line was a long round now shows in the player lists again.

Behind the scenes: renaming a player, saving map tiles and reading what the game's pages send are all done more safely, and a few things are tidied away when a round or the app stops. Nothing should play differently.

"Plays like" (beside the wind on the course and the range target) now comes from the game's own ball flight: into the wind it says more for a short iron than before (a 7-iron into 20 mph plays about a third longer, not a fifth), and warm air takes off only a yard or two, not ten.
A soft chip landing on a barely sloping green now checks up as it does on a flat one - it lost speed it shouldn't have.
Stroke play scores part way through a round are ranked on how far over or under par each player is, so someone a hole behind isn't shown leading just for having fewer strokes.

A launch monitor sending numbers no golf shot has (a 400 mph ball, a launch straight up) is ignored rather than played, and a stray character on the connection no longer stops every shot after it getting through.
Behind the scenes: missing numbers in a shot or a green's speed can no longer break a flight or a putt, and old shots are judged against your counted shots only. Nothing should play differently.

Some saved courses change a little where they were wrong, and are now the same for everyone and every load: a tree standing on a fairway you added by hand to another hole goes, a path between holes moves round a pond or bunker you added where it ran (and taking a hole's own paths out no longer takes those with it), and another hole's woods look the same whichever hole you see them from.
A par 4 or 5 given a very short length no longer turns back on itself behind the tee.

Behind the scenes: courses load the same way every time (a routing remembered from earlier in a session is no longer used for a slightly different course), hand edits far off a hole or a damaged course file can't stall the game, and working out the holes around you is quicker. Nothing should play differently.

Handicaps on a course of fewer than 18 holes (other than 9) now give that share of the strokes, as ladder matches already did, and strokes always fall on the same holes when only some have a stroke index.
A ladder handicap no longer says "held back from rising too fast" for ever once it has been.
On an online ladder you can challenge the same player at most three times a day (taking a challenge back and sending it again sent them an alert each time).

Behind the scenes: the online play relay makes its codes more securely, answers bad requests properly, keeps its pages at the edge better, stops a connection that floods it with messages, and no longer stores anything when someone asks about a code nobody has. Nothing should play differently.
Windows app: Go back to the previous version is only offered while that version can still be downloaded, and if going back fails a window says so (before, nothing seemed to happen).
Windows app: a program to start with A² Golf that's a .bat or .cmd file in a folder with spaces in its name now starts, and one that stops straight away says it didn't start rather than that it did.
Windows app: a game page that keeps crashing as it loads is tried again less and less often instead of every second, and the app starting a second time no longer touches the first one's settings.
Behind the scenes: the build and release steps are stricter about failing loudly and about what they're allowed to change. Nothing should play differently.

Behind the scenes: tidying - every script is now checked by the tests (and by ESLint for names used that don't exist), line endings are fixed in place, a stray recording is gone from the code, and the online play tests pick free ports. Nothing should play differently.

The game starts up more smoothly the first time you click: its sounds are got ready a few at a time, and the long background loops (water, wind, rain, the outdoor bed) only when they're first heard. Those loops now go round without a seam, as the cart's already did.

Behind the scenes: a little graphics memory that wasn't given back now is (the sky's reflection, some repeated shapes), a warning if the 3D library ever changes the sky in a way the game doesn't expect, and tidier tests. Nothing should look or play differently.

Online play: if the host's connection hiccups, the other bays now join back in their own places by themselves instead of being stuck on "join again", and a dropped host's game code can only be taken over by a bay from that game.

Behind the scenes: the online play relay now shares its free daily allowance more fairly (an idle host costs very little, and one connection can't use it all up), forgets ladders, seasons and phone links nobody has used for a long time, and keeps what a browser hands your PC until the PC has it. Nothing should play differently.

A shot that's plainly another club - a drive with the 7 iron still picked - is now counted as the club it flew like straight away, and on the range that club is picked for your next shot too. Z, or saying "undo", puts both back.

A distance you leave unanswered no longer becomes a club's normal when it's another of your clubs' distance, and a club with another club's shots mixed into it is judged by a typical bag until it's sorted - so wrong ones keep being caught.

My stats has a new Wrong club? section: it looks through all your shots for ones that flew like another club, groups a session of them together, and moves them, keeps them, or marks them bad hits or misreads in one tap - with Undo. The shots put right by themselves are listed there too, to put back.

Voice is simpler: to begin with it's just for changing club, the last shot - "Caddie, last shot seven iron", "last shot mishit", "good", "misread" - and answering what's asked, each done straight away with no "say confirm". Notes, powers, replays, scenes, the putting green and the rest are under Menu, Sound & voice, More voice commands.
With voice on, a shot that flew like another club asks - "Your 7 iron flew like a driver - the driver? Say yes, no or mishit" - and you just answer out loud, no wake word needed.

Keep your stats in your own Google Drive: on My stats, under Your Google account, sign in with Google and each player's stats are kept there and in step on every computer they sign in on - shots played with no internet go once it's back. For now only for testers the game's owner has added.

Sign in to play: the first time A² Golf opens it asks you to sign in - with Google (your stats and players then go with you to the phone and the web) or an email and password - then which player you are. After that it opens straight into you every time. Click the player's name to switch to someone else signed in, sign another person in, add friends and guests (no sign-in needed for them), or sign out.

Behind the scenes: holes get ready quicker again - working out the holes round the one you are playing takes about half the time it did after the last update, building a hole about a fifth less, and a hole from a real course map lays out its grass a quarter quicker. Nothing should play or look differently.
Behind the scenes: the web test of A² Golf now has a home - the online play relay's own address. Nothing should play differently.

The cart between holes no longer drives through signs, benches, bins, the windsock, gorse bushes or rocks - including the arrow pointing on to the next tee - on the path or off it, and parks clear of them.
Behind the scenes: a first test of A² Golf in a web browser, for iPhones and anyone without the app. Nothing should play differently.

Behind the scenes: holes get ready quicker - working out the other holes and woods round the one you're playing takes about half the time it did, and building a hole about a fifth less. Nothing should play or look differently.

Seasons by post: a season for friends who aren't on at the same time. Make one in the Online tab's Seasons - how many events, how many days each stays open, 9 or 18 holes, gross or net - and send its link in WhatsApp or an email, or show its QR code. Anyone with it joins in a tap.

Each event in a season by post is open for its days: play your round whenever you like before it closes, in one go, with the same tees, cups, weather and bounces as everyone else. Its leaderboard fills up as the rounds come in, and the season's table adds up the points as each event closes.
A season by post has its own web page anyone can open from its link - the events with their deadlines, the leaderboards and the table - with a button that opens A² Golf ready to join.
The Online tab no longer empties a form you're filling in on Ladders or Seasons a few seconds after it opens.

Online ladders can now wait to fill up: give a new Live or Postal ladder 4, 6, 8, 12 or 16 places, and everyone who joins gets a place straight away - nobody has to let them in. When the last place goes the ladder starts by itself, with the rungs drawn, and everyone with alerts hears it's under way. The ladder's maker can start it sooner with Start now.

New on the Online tab's Ladders: Open ladders - ladders anyone playing A² Golf can join, made with Who can join: Anyone. Find one that suits how you swing and your handicap, and press Join to take a place. Strangers only see names, and can only say the set lines.

Every online ladder now has its own page on the web, the link Share the link sends. It works on any phone or computer with no app, showing the places filled or the ladder, the matches waiting and the latest results, with buttons to open it in the phone app or in A² Golf on your PC.

Sign a phone's browser in to your PC (On the web, on the Online tab's Ladders, then scan the QR code) and that browser shows your ladders. From a ladder's page you can join as one of your players, or answer a Live challenge, and it goes on your PC the next time A² Golf is open.
On Windows, a match ladder's or an online game's link clicked in WhatsApp, an email or a browser now opens A² Golf at it, ready to join.
Watch highlights now shows each highlight on its own hole with just that shot: before, every clip flew the round's last hole's shots again first, so they all looked like the same hole.
Phone app: Turns with the phone (Menu, Screens) now does what it says - the app was never actually told your choice, so it went on turning every way.
Fixed an error behind the scenes when the putting line's setting was changed before the putting green had been visited.

Behind the scenes: a report now says which part of the game a slow moment was spent in (the cart ride, the putt's read, the recording and so on), and after a crash it lists more of what was going on when it happened, so slowdowns and crashes can be tracked down. Nothing should play differently.

Choosing a course is now a course picker: press the course in the Course tab, then type any part of its name or what kind of course you want (links, hilly, by the sea, 9 holes) and narrow it with filters for holes, look, ground, the sea, where it came from and whether you have played it - each showing how many courses it leaves - in the order you like.
New course and Real course from the map are at the foot of the course picker, and the course designer's own list of courses can be searched and filtered the same way.
The Course tab no longer has anything for online play: hosting, joining and the online ladders are all on the Online tab.
On the phone, the Course tab no longer offers the course designer, which only showed an error there.
On the phone, the app tells you when a newer version is out, with a Download button - it installs over the old one and keeps your rounds.

On the phone, the game now turns with you: hold the phone upright and the picture fills the top of the screen, with the swing pad and the buttons in a dock underneath, under your thumb. Turn it back sideways any time - your round, putt or session carries on.
Held upright, the camera stands back a little so you can still see down the hole, the shot numbers run across the bottom of the picture, and the side panel comes up where the swing pad was.
New in Menu, Screens: Turns with the phone - keep the game sideways only or upright only, so a tilt while you swing never turns it.
On the phone held upright, the loading screen is now in the middle of the screen.

Online seasons, played together: in the Online tab's new Seasons, make a season of 4 to 10 events on your courses, gross or net, and play each event with your friends from the lobby. Everyone in the game sees the standings - 500 points for a win, 300 for second and so on.

The graphics settings have new names, one step down: Standard is now Very low, Medium is Low, High is Standard and Ultra is Medium. Your setting is the same picture under its new name (the game says so once), and it makes room above for a new High and Ultra later.

Trees along the front of a wood now grow towards the light, as real ones do: their crowns fuller and reaching out on the open side over the rough towards the fairway - and a ball meets them just where they're drawn. They never reach out over another hole.

New trees: clumps of two to four silver birches from one base, alders grown in a clump of stems (mostly by the water), old pines gone flat across the top and low, broad-headed broadleaves under the big trees. Holes you've already played keep their trees as they were; the new ones grow on holes you haven't played yet, or after Grow its trees afresh in the hole editor.

When a round counted for something, the standings come up beside the round card at the end: your season, an online season, the online match over several games or a match ladder - the top five and your players, in gold. The recording's Finish scene shows them too.

Behind the scenes: the green and the ground under it are drawn with less wasted work round the cup, and the next hole is built ahead in smaller pieces, so the picture stays smoother while you play. Nothing should play differently.

Heathland courses' bunkers are now fingered: long fingers of sand reaching up the bunker's face into the turf, with tongues of grass between them, as at Sunningdale or Pine Valley - and now and then a parkland green has one too. They play exactly as they're drawn, down to each finger.

Cross bunkers: a three-shot par 5's bunker across the lay-up is now a row of bunkers right across the fairway - carry it or lay up - and on heathland and links holes now and then a row waits where the long hitters' drives finish, with a gap at one end on the hole's better side.

Waste areas - big stretches of sandy, scrubby ground with heather, gorse, stones and tufts - now play as their own lie, Waste area: firm sand the ball sits up on, no bunker rules, nearly a fairway shot. They're on heathland holes and now and then out in a links hole's rough.
On the range, lie practice can hit from a waste area too.
The ready-made courses are given again with the new bunkers and waste areas where they fit (one you've changed is kept as your copy).

Behind the scenes: the WebGPU test (Menu, Screens) now draws the whole driving range with the new renderer just as the game draws it today - the screen effects, the sand and spray a ball throws up and, on Medium, the living water and the trees mirrored in it, the clouds in three dimensions and the motes in the sunlight - so the frame rates it shows compare like with like. Nothing should play differently.

The frame rate on the PC now shows just the frames a second, as on the phone, so it no longer stretches across the top of the picture. Click it for the rest - the frame time, the slowest frame, what each frame draws, the picture and the setting - and click again to shut it.

Feedback for everyone: Menu, System, Feedback saves a report of what happened on your PC and opens the support page with your note filled in - drag the report on and post it. Nothing is sent until you do.

The installer now shows the licence agreement, and is called A-Squared-Golf-Setup. The licence, a privacy note saying what stays on your PC and what's sent when, and the credits for everything the game is built with are in Menu, Help, About.
Feedback has sensible limits: a note needs a sentence, there's a short wait between reports, and up to 5 a day.

On the phone, the app opens straight into the game - no Play or At the range screen to get past first, so you're playing sooner. It always opens for playing on the phone with your finger. For a range session with your launch monitor, go to Menu, Play, Range session; End range session (in the menu, or on the Session card) takes you back to phone play.

Grass no longer stands on the cart paths, on the phone as well as the PC: every tuft and clump of long grass, and the heather, gorse and flowers, keep off each path right where it's drawn - the next hole's path the cart drives along, the joined-up bends and the gravel ends included.

The cart between holes minds its manners: it no longer drives down or across the fairway of the hole you've just played - where it has to cross over to the next hole it goes round the back of the green, out of the way of players behind. It takes a clear gap through the trees instead of going a long way round them, and no longer goes a long way back down the cart path when the next tee is the other way.

The frame rate is back on the game screen if it had gone missing: anything moved off the picture is brought back onto it. On the game screen the frame rate now sits under the top line on the right, with the hole map and messages below it, so the microphone and connection stay at the right end of the top line.

Arranging the game screen (Shift + B) now lists everything that can show there - what's showing, what's off and when the rest appear - so you can turn the frame rate or key tips back on, or put anything back where it started.
In the command centre, Arrange lists the boxes you've taken out (a camera, the Last shot, Shot history, Keys or Game screen) - tick one to bring it back.
The Online tab has a cleaner look: one size of text, the sections along the top with a close button, Host and Join side by side, and the ladders and host rules laid out neatly.

The game starts much quicker, above all on Ultra: the graphics it prepares as it starts are kept from one start to the next and used again, where before they were made afresh every time the sun had moved (the first start after this update still makes them once). The range is built a little quicker too, and preparing the picture starts sooner.

Cart paths that meet now join as one path: where one path carries on from the end of another - a hole's own, one between holes, the next hole's - it's drawn as one continuous path, its edges and kerbs lining up, and where one runs into the side of another the kerbs open and the tarmac runs on from one to the other. Paths no longer have rounded ends: where a path stops, the tarmac breaks up into gravel that thins out into the grass. The worn grass along a path fades away where it meets a fairway, a tee or another path, instead of stopping square. Tight bends in a path are drawn as smooth curves, so their inside edge no longer folds over.
Marram grass and rabbit scrapes on links holes keep off the cart paths, as the rest of the grass does.

Trees: two new shapes each for pines and broadleaves, the commonest trees - a wind-shorn pine, a tall narrow spire, a broadleaf grown from an old coppice and a tall upright one - so a wood has more variety. Trees from a real course's measurements, or planted as a kind, now vary a little in height and in how wide they spread, rather than every one standing exactly as measured.

A new picture effect, Finer leaves (on High and Ultra): the trees near you are drawn with more, smaller leaves, so a close tree reads as leaves rather than as cards of them. Turn it off for fewer, larger cards, as before.

A new picture effect on Ultra, Fewer pixels, built up over time (with Smooth edges over time on): the picture is drawn at two-thirds of its size each way and the full-size picture is built up from the last few frames - nearly as sharp, for under half the drawing.
On the phone, the small pieces of each hole's ground, bunkers and paths that look alike are drawn together, so there is less for the phone to send to its graphics chip each frame.

With the frame rate showing, the line along the top of the game screen - the player, the club, the result, the microphone and the connection - now stops short of it, so nothing is hidden under the frame rate box.
The command centre's top bar fits on one row again on a 1440 px screen now there's an Online tab, and if yours slipped onto two rows it goes back to one by itself (unless you placed it by hand).

Recording: the Swing review and YouTube layouts are new. Swing review has every number along the bottom, eight to a row, and no title box. YouTube edges the game in yellow, moves who's hitting to the top right, and shows eight big numbers down the left once the ball lands. A Swing review or YouTube layout you never changed becomes the new one by itself; one you changed stays as it is.

Water and unplayable balls: every option the Rules of Golf give you is marked on the hole before you choose - back where you played from, back on the line from the hole, or within two club-lengths (red water and unplayable balls). Then you pick the spot yourself: as far back on the line as you like, or anywhere in the two club-lengths, with the arrows, a click, a finger or the controller. The card tells you the lie, whether trees are in the way and the yards to go before you drop. Out of the water you now choose too, instead of the game dropping it for you.
The game's own drop out of the water (in a scramble, or for another bay's ball) no longer lands in the long grass or trees just behind the water when there's grass a few yards further back.

The cart between holes now drives all the way to the next tee - the one you are playing from - along the cart paths wherever they go its way, and parks beside the tee box. It waits by the green you have just played, never somewhere random, and on a long way it drives a little quicker so it is always there in time.

A new Online tab in the top bar, after Challenges, holds everything you play against other people online. Play now is where you host or join a game. Ladders has your online match ladders, live or by post, and a new one starts as Live. Host rules has the rules for a game you host: line reads, the mouse and controller level, skill points and carry adjustments, moved there from the course panel. A number on the tab says when something's waiting on your ladders. The course panel keeps your round, seasons and the ladders you play at the bay or against made-up golfers. On the phone, Play's Play with friends and Match ladders tiles are now one Online tile.
Making an online ladder when the game can't reach the online server now tells you so, instead of quietly making a ladder against made-up golfers.

Match ladders: the game's questions (delete a ladder, play a match, end a round or a season) now ask in the game's own box, so the New ladder form no longer gets stuck after you say no - you can start a Live ladder straight away. Online ladders have Leave: you come off the ladder for everyone, an admin hands it over to another player first, and the last one out ends it. A ladder match you left or that's already played no longer turns your next online game into that match.

Your phone and your PC now share players and stats. Link the phone once: on the PC, My stats then Your phones then Link a phone shows a code and a QR code; on the phone, open My stats (on Play and At the range) and scan the QR code or type the code. After that they keep in step by themselves, even when they are never on at the same time: the shots and rounds you play on the phone go into your PC's stats, and your PC's players, handicaps, skill points, club distances and last rounds come to the phone. The same name is the same player on both, and a player you add on the phone joins your PC's saved players. Up to six phones, and either side can unlink. This replaces the phone's Send to your PC and the code you typed each time.
Recording designer: pick several boxes (Shift + click) and change them all at once - text size, backing, colours, outline, corners, border - or, for a box in a group, its whole group or just it.
Recording designer: exact numbers beside every size - text size, outline and border thickness, corners in pixels, how solid as a percentage - so every border can be exactly 5 pixels, say.

Recording designer: put boxes in a container (Down, Across or A grid) and they are laid out evenly inside it, the same size with an even gap and padding you can set in pixels; size or move the container and they follow.

Recording designer: crop the game or a camera as in OBS - hold Alt and drag an edge to cut the picture there without moving it (a square part of a 4:3 game, say), or type how much to cut from each side; Whole picture puts it back.

Recordings keep the game picture centred on the target line even when the picture centre is moved for play ([ and ]), while the game screen stays exactly as it is. Turn it off with the Game view setting Centred on the target line.

On the phone: Ultra's clouds are soft puffs instead of speckled 3D clouds; when it's running slowly the graphics ease themselves down much sooner, and say so; and no keyboard keys are shown or mentioned anywhere on its screens.
The replay card after a hole is now just a small Replay button, and it fades away 10 seconds after you finish the hole (J still replays it until your next shot).

Fixes you can see: on Ultra, the grass on a bank by the green no longer shows as light patches with straight edges - each clump is lit like the slope it grows on; no grass on the cart path as the cart drives to the next tee; and on Sea Links' 2nd the two overlapping pot bunkers on the left are one bunker.
When the Omni's Bluetooth drops, it comes back sooner: one quick try to reconnect, then a fresh search straight away. It used to spend about 20 more seconds on a second try that never worked.
Reports to Claude after a graphics crash now say what crashed and which graphics driver your PC has, from Windows' own crash file. That file stays on your PC; nothing extra is sent.

Match ladders on the phone: Play's Match ladders tile opens your ladders in the side panel, the same as on the PC - challenge, answer, play and see results - and says when something's waiting for you.
Join an online ladder by QR code: QR code by the ladder's code shows one to point a phone's camera at, or Share the link to send. The phone app opens on the join with the code typed in.
Say something with a challenge - one of a few set lines like Good luck! or Rematch? - on a match waiting to be played, and after a result. Both players see it under the match.
Postal ladder: once both rounds are in, Watch their round lists the other player's shots hole by hole beside yours.
Phone alerts for ladders (a challenge, an answer, a line said, a Postal round in), once they're switched on for the app - until then the app works as before.

The cart ride between holes no longer gets stuck on Loading: the next hole gets ready much faster while you watch the cart, Next hole always works, and if the hole isn't quite ready a short loading card finishes it.

Android app: before a round the side panel comes out by itself with the course, the game, your ladders and Start round, and the touch strip and swing pad stay out of the way until there's a ball to hit. Fewer boxes on top of each other: the range's Session button sits in the touch strip, the strip stays below the top bar, and the swing pad moves aside when the side panel is open.
Android app: the top bar comes back with a tap or a pull down on its tab, now bigger and just below the top edge - swiping down from the very top edge is left to Android's own notifications.

Android app: the side panel's sections fold away to their headings until you tap one, so it opens as a short list with Match ladder near the top - and a folded Match ladder says how many things are waiting there.

Android app: the next hole is built much sooner while you stand over the ball - every moment the picture is still goes on it, starting a second or two into each hole - so far fewer loading cards between holes.

Smoother graphics with nothing looking different: the ground under the fairway, green and tee is no longer coloured twice (once for the rough beneath it), the sky is only worked out where you can see it, High and Ultra no longer work out the soft shadows on the ground in front of you twice over, and on Ultra the edge smoothing is lighter where the picture is already smoothed twice - which also frees some of the graphics card's memory.
The Replay button after a hole has a ring round it that runs down to nothing as its 10 seconds go, so you can see when it'll disappear.

Pick the time of day beside the sky - Morning, Midday, Afternoon, Late afternoon, From the clock, or Any for a surprise each round (the range has the same choice) - and it moves on about 15 minutes a hole, the sun with it: each hole says the time, and the round card shows when you teed off and finished. Nobody plays in the dark: From the clock tees off now unless the round would run past sunset, then starts earlier so your last hole ends as the light goes (by the real sunset for the date in the UK), and Late afternoon always ends at dusk.

The sky is no longer always blue: as evening sets in the horizon turns gold and orange towards the sun, with pink and mauve on the far side, the clouds and the haze warm and the sunlight goes golden; an early round starts in a paler, pinker dawn that fades to blue as the sun climbs.

The sky changes from round to round: a clear day can have no clouds at all, and on a day of sunny spells there might be a few clouds or plenty, their shadows drifting over the course to match (the range has its own each visit). The clouds look softer too - each puff's edge broken up, and a cloud that's going thins away as a whole instead of leaving rings of puffs.

Everything looks more natural: the grass is a real fairway's green instead of a bright neon one, the trees and leaves softer, the sky still blue and the flags red, and the darkest shade under the trees and in the rough keeps its detail rather than going black.

Each round the course is in its own season and kept its own way: today's season most rounds and the one either side on others, and anywhere from lush and green to dry and browning - drier on a links or with firm fairways, lusher after rain - with the greens and tees always kept watered.

Water looks real: the sea reflects the sky out to a crisp horizon; ponds are glassy in the shelter of the bank and choppier out on open water, and never turn pitch black on a calm day; burns and brooks run downstream over a stony bed, their cut banks broken earth with the turf slumping over; and the ponds on the holes around you reflect the sky too.

New: match ladders, in the course panel's Match ladder section. Play one against one, match play, on a ladder of rungs: challenge someone up to three rungs above you, and if you beat them you take their rung. Play friends at the bay, taking turns, or play a solo ladder against nine made-up golfers around your handicap, who also play each other every week.

Before a ladder match a card shows the odds, who gets strokes and on which holes, and the rung at stake. The match is over as soon as it's decided (5&4), with the ladder's own gimmes and level, no mulligans and no skill points. Afterwards everyone's rating moves, and a handicap ladder keeps a handicap made only from ladder matches. Each month's champion is whoever's on rung 1 at the end.

New: online match ladders - the Live ladder. Make one in the Match ladder section (Play: Live) and send its code to friends in other houses; they join with it and you let them in. Challenge someone, they accept on a course of their choice, then they host the match as an online game straight from the ladder and you join it from yours. When it's decided, both bays send the result and it goes on the ladder.

New: the Postal ladder - an online ladder where each of you plays the match on your own, whenever you like within the week. The one challenged picks the course when they accept, and you both play the very same round: the same tees, cups and weather, and even the same luck shot for shot. It is one go, with no restarts (if the game closes part way, carry on from the next hole). Neither sees the other's scores until both rounds are in - then the reveal shows both, hole by hole, with the match as it went.

Match ladders: an honours board of every season's champion, and rivalries - the card before a match says your head-to-head, and a result can say more: a giant-killing, a third defence in a row, a third win in a row. On an online ladder you can say you're away for up to four weeks (no challenges, no slipping), the panel warns you after two weeks without a match, and when the game opens a message says if a challenge or a match is waiting for you.
Online play by code: a friend joining a game on a large course could be left waiting for the course and never start the round. Big courses now reach every bay.

The shot setup is now two pictures: a ball with a dot for the spin and the curve (drag it left or right to curve the shot, lower for more backspin) and a bar for the height, any amount rather than set steps. Each is green in the middle, then amber, then red, with the risk said under it: a little costs nothing, and the further out you go the more a crooked swing is punished. Open it with the little Shot ball beside the swing pad (phone and mouse) or Y on a controller - the left stick moves the dot, the D-pad changes the height, A is done and X puts it back to a plain shot.

Swinging with a finger, the mouse or a controller is much easier at Beginner and Amateur - more room either side of where to stop, a little wobble forgiven, fewer bad strikes and less scatter - and Pro and Tour are a bit harder, where pulling too far now costs a lot. Half power (½) lasts for one swing, so the next drive isn't a half one by mistake.

Two lines on the swing pad at Beginner and Amateur: a dashed white one for the flag as if it were flat, still and from the fairway, and a blue one for where to stop as the shot really plays - into or with the wind, up or downhill, in cold or warm air, out of the rough - with the reason at the foot of the pad; on the green, the hole's line and the putt's pace. They show on the course, on the range when you aim at a target and in the approach challenges, and never ask for more than a full swing.

Your level is always on show at the top of the swing pad, green for Beginner through to red for Tour; tap it to see the four side by side - Beginner and Amateur forgive mistakes but hit shorter, Pro and Tour punish them but hit further. Two good rounds at your level and you move up one by itself (1 of 2 good rounds towards Amateur shows under Level, on the phone's Your level and in Saved players); go back down any time, or turn it off in Menu, Swing pad & controller. Before a round the card says each player's level, with Change level.

Test shot has gone - the top bar button, the space bar, the menu item and the controller and phone buttons. To play without a launch monitor, swing with the mouse on the swing pad, a finger or a game controller; the shot data screen says mouse swing or controller swing under those shots, and the course panel's online rule for them is now called Mouse and controller online.

Online play has 25 reactions, picked from a wheel that puts the ones that fit first - Get up! while a friend's ball is in the air, Birdie! or Hole in one! when it drops, Splash!, Timber! or Beach day!, So close!, Good luck! and Good game. Tap the button and then one, or press, slide and let go. They stay on screen for 20 seconds and stack at the right of the picture. With separate screens the lobby opens on the command centre, with the reactions button in its top bar.

Online play: watch a friend's shot from where they stand. Watch beside their name in the side panel puts your camera behind their ball and follows the shot through the air; Next goes to the next friend and Back to my ball comes back - as it does by itself when you swing, when they finish the hole and at the next hole.

Online play's lobby shows everyone's level beside their name, with Levels... to change yours before the start, and the host's rules - including the easiest level anyone plays at - for everyone who's joined. With separate screens the levels card opens in the command centre, and the host's Play list no longer runs off the panel.

The cart ride between holes now follows the cart as it drives to the next tee, instead of going straight in to its screen. Press Scorecard, or tap the picture, to look up at the scorecard on the cart's screen, and Watch the drive to go back out.

Android app: Home has moved into the menu, at the top, and the home screens have Back to the game. The top bar slides out of the way while you play, so the game has the whole screen - pull down from the top, or tap the little tab, to bring it back, or turn on Top bar always shown in Menu, Screens.

The phone app runs more smoothly, drawing less of what its small screen can't show - simpler range balls, lighter tree shading, full-detail trees only near you and the ball's flight - so on the range it draws about half as much while you line up. The PC's range balls are simpler too, at no difference you can see.

Phone app, at the range: a Session button shows your session so far - every shot, each club's distances (average carry, shortest to longest, how wide) and, when you finish, a summary: shots and minutes, your longest, your straightest club, and any two clubs that go the same distance or leave a big gap.

Phone app: the Omni comes back by itself if it drops - straight back to the one you had, and at once when you return to the app - and the top bar says Reconnecting to the Omni meanwhile (on the PC too).

Recording designer (and the scene designer page): the Add list shows each number, tile and piece of information as it looks in the game; Before the shot, In flight and After it lands hide what isn't shown then; Preview shows the scene full size; and better framing - Thirds and Safe area guides that boxes snap to, Frame it buttons for a half, a corner, a strip or the whole picture, and Even gaps and matching Borders and corners for several boxes.

The boxes over the picture keep out of each other's way at every screen size, on one screen and on the separate game screen: the frame rate box is in the top right corner clear of your strokes and score, the messages symbol off the hole map, the hole's note and lie lines beside the swing pad, the bar for watching a friend just above the numbers, a ladder challenge's ladder beside a left-hand swing pad, and on the phone the card before a round and the words along the top clear of the Shot and ½ buttons.

Fixes you can see: bunkers that overlap are one bunker, with no line across the sand and no sky showing through where they meet (as on Nine Oaks' 1st and Sea Links' 2nd), and no slits of sky at the tight ends of long bunkers; from above, parkland hay no longer looks like rows of pale bricks and other holes' bunkers don't show their fairway through the sand; the next hole's cart path is no longer hidden under the grass until close, and from Links by the Sea's 7th it crosses the burn on a bridge; and on Ultra the frame rate box's draws and triangles no longer jump about beside a pond.

Playing online, a Lobby button now sits at the start of the top bar once the game has started (next to Home on the phone), whatever you're playing. If you're hosting, it stops the game and takes everyone back to the lobby to pick the next game - it asks first, unless the round is over. On everyone else's screen it opens the online play panel, to see who's playing or leave the game. On a phone held upright, the top bar now always fits on the screen: who's playing and where you are get cut short rather than the menu going off the edge.

On parkland holes the long grass and the pale, waist-high hay are now always there, however far off or high up the camera is, instead of growing up out of the ground as the camera comes towards them. They're drawn very simply far off, so it costs little.

Online play has a lot more to it. In the lobby each bay presses I'm ready, the host sees who they're still waiting for, and Start counts down five seconds on every screen so nobody is still finding their club. Once a game's over the host can press Rematch to play the same again.

Quick reactions when playing online: a button at the bottom left of the picture sends Nice shot!, Great shot!, Unlucky!, a laugh, Wow! or Good game to every bay's screen. Each bay can send one every 30 seconds.
In an online round the scores beside the map are now a live leaderboard, everyone in order with their places. Bars beside each player in the online play panel show how good their connection is.

The host can pause an online game for everyone, and carry on when ready. They can also save the game they've set up by name to pick again next time, and start a match over several games, with a points table everyone can see.

If the host's connection goes for good in a game played by code, the next bay takes over as host and the game carries on. If a bay's game restarts part way through a round it picks up where it was, and after the app starts again the online play panel offers to rejoin the game.
The host's code now comes with a QR code: a friend points their phone's camera at it to open the game's code in the A² Golf phone app.
On parkland holes the ground under the drifts of hay is now straw-coloured as well, so a drift reads clearly as hay from far away.

Oaks near you are each their own tree now too, with their own boughs, as the broadleaves have been. Every tree's colour is now its own: the same tree is the same shade from its own hole and from the next, and no longer changes when trees round it are added or cleared. A ball now brushes the leaves on a tree's boughs where they reach out past the rest of its crown.

The golf cart now sounds like a real one, still quietly: its wheels rolling and its electric motor humming, a touch higher and louder the faster it goes and duller on the grass than on the path, and now and then the clubs rattling in the bag on the back, never on a beat. You can add your own in the sounds folder: in the folders cart (rolling), cart-motor (the motor) and cart-rattle (the clubs).

A course's trees now stay as they are from one game to the next. The first time you play a hole, where each of its trees stands and how it grew (its kind, shape, size and lean), its bushes and the trees behind its green are kept with the course on your PC, and the hole is grown from them every time after - so a new version of the game no longer moves or changes them. Only how trees are drawn (their leaves and boughs) gets better with new versions. Changes you make in the hole editor still go on top; a hole remade in the designer, or given its trees from LiDAR, grows afresh and is kept again. Online, everyone sees the host's trees.

Silver birches near you are each their own tree now too: slender boughs rise steeply off their limbs and arch over, their fine twigs hanging in loose clouds of small leaves, with the white branches showing between them - so each birch has its own outline and none is the same as the next.

Pines, Scots pines and spruces near you are each their own tree now too: sprays of needles reach out from the trunk to the edge of each tier, more or fewer, further or less, all round or crowded to one side, so no two have the same outline. A ball meets their needles just as before.

The golf cart between holes now waits right by the green you've just played and makes a short drive on towards the next tee, stopping beside it when it's near, instead of driving all the way there. It keeps well away from trees and long grass, at least 4 metres from both wherever it can, and no longer cuts across the long grass round a green or under the edges of trees. Holes that used to have no cart ride now get one.

Cart paths now join up from one hole to the next: where a hole's path ends past its green and the next hole's path starts behind its tee, a path now runs between them, round greens, tees and sand, over a brook on a little bridge rather than round it, along a path that's there already rather than beside it, and never across another hole's play. Where the way between them would be long or would cross another hole, the one path simply ends and the next starts again, and the carts drive over the grass. The courses that come with the game have these paths between holes now, as new courses always did.

Cart paths look tidier: a path now crosses a brook or burn straight over on a bridge instead of going all the way round its end, two holes' paths running side by side a few metres apart now share one path, and a hole's path no longer runs over another hole's tee, green or bunkers (it goes round them, or stops short and starts again past them). The grass either side of every path is kept short for 2 metres instead of long grass growing right up to its edge, and no tree hangs out over a path. A few trees whose crowns reached over a path have been taken away, on courses you've played before too.

In the hole editor, Trees (with no trees picked) has a new Grow its trees afresh button: the next time you play the hole, its trees, bushes and the trees behind its green grow as this version of the game grows them, and are kept that way from then on. Undo puts the old ones back until you play it.

Every other tree and shrub near you is its own now too: a Lombardy poplar's short, upright boughs run all the way up its column; a weeping willow's boughs arch out of its dome, each hanging its own curtain of leaves; bushes and flowering shrubs have small sprigs poking out of them here and there; a dark column conifer has the odd tuft poking out of its side; and a dead tree has bare boughs of its own forking off its branches.

On High and Ultra each tree now keeps its own outline at any distance: from the tee you see the same boughs, crowded to the same side, as when you walk past it, instead of one of a few standard shapes until you get close. The trees in the far woods out in the country have boughs in their pictures too.
Close up, an oak's or plane tree's boughs now wear its own leaves instead of a jumble of tiny leaves of every kind.

On High, trees hidden behind the ones lining the hole keep their plain shape further off, which saves drawing. They put on their own boughs as soon as you line up a shot that could go near them, before the ball gets there.

The paths between holes, and each hole's own paths as you play them, are now kept with the course: worked out once - when you save a course in the designer, when a course that comes with the game is first added, or the first time you play any other - and the same every time after, so a new version of the game no longer moves them. They're worked out again only when you change the holes they join.

In the hole editor the Paths tool now shows the paths to and from the holes either side, in yellow, and you can change them from either hole: tap one, then drag its line to bend it or a white dot to move that bit, take a bend out, put it back as worked out, or have no path between those two holes (a button brings it back). A path between holes still can't go over a tee, a green or sand, or along water rather than over it on a bridge.

A tee box no longer sits on another hole's green: on Sea Links the 9th's white tee was on the 8th green, so you saw it there as you played into that green. Where there's no room behind a tee for its white box, the whites play from the yellow tee.

The game's own videos are replaced by one: Menu, Cameras & video, Record the A² Golf video (or say "record the show reel"). The game plays it by itself and records it, just under four minutes long: a tee shot on each kind of hole, approaches and putts, a hole in one, four friends playing a hole online - their drives coming straight at you, then all four putting at once - and the course designer changing a hole in a few taps. Nothing it does is kept, and the game is back as it was when it ends. Esc stops it.

The golf cart no longer whines. It now plays a recording of a real electric golf cart, quietly, a touch higher and louder the faster it goes; until a cart recording is in the game, you only hear its tyres. You can add your own cart recordings in the sounds folder, in a folder called cart.
Finish for YouTube's trailer.mp4 is no longer a black screen in Windows' own video player: the picture is now made H.264, which every player and YouTube take, whatever format the game recorded in.

Broadleaves near you are each their own tree now (a first try): instead of eight shapes turned and sized, each grows its own boughs off its limbs - more or fewer, reaching further or less, high or low, even all round or crowded to one side - each ending in big clumps of leaves of its own shade. It takes a little more than a megabyte of memory.

Trees: more variety, at no cost to the frame rate. Trees near each other now share a cast, one stand a little yellower and lighter and the next bluer and darker, carrying on into the woods behind; a tree out in the open is a little lighter and warmer than one deep in a wood; every crown is mottled its own way; there are more shades of green (lime, blue-green, a silver-blue spruce, a silvery poplar and more); and about one tree in seven is a young one, smaller and slimmer.

The golf cart between holes now drives like one: its wheels turn as it goes and the front two steer round the bends, and you can hear it - an electric cart's whine rising as it picks up speed and dying away as it coasts to a stop, and its tyres hissing along the path or swishing through the grass. Still no one in it but you.

Trees play more like real trees. A crown is mostly air: a ball can go right through one barely touched, glance off a branch and carry on, kick up, out to the side or back off it, or - in the thick of a big tree - be knocked down. The leaves alone no longer take most of its speed, and the edge of a tree hardly slows it. The result line says which ("Off a branch", "Through the leaves"), and the warning before a shot from under the trees now says how likely the branches are to catch it.

Finish for YouTube (Menu, Play, Videos, or the button after the Launch trailer is recorded): puts your music under the trailer, cuts four upright Shorts and writes the description with chapters and your download link - all in the game, in a folder beside the recording. It needs ffmpeg once: in PowerShell, winget install ffmpeg.
Online play: a friend's shot now flies on your screen as they hit it, not once it has landed at their end - no more waiting a few seconds to see it.

Online play: everyone goes on to the next hole together. Next hole (or the scorecard or cart ride moving on by itself) says you're ready, and the next hole starts for everyone once all are - till then the card says who you're waiting for.

Online play: the host can stop the game and take everyone back to the lobby, still in with the same code, then start the next game - another course, putting, chipping, golf pong or a Challenge - and everyone is taken to it.
Online play: at the end of the round the host's scorecard has Back to the lobby, taking everyone back to pick the next game; everyone else's says who they're waiting for.

Online play: you're told when someone joins, drops out, comes back or leaves, and joining no longer waits while your handicaps are looked up. Everyone needs this version to play together - the PC app and the phone app alike.

Cart paths no longer run through trees: trees that belonged to a neighbouring hole could stand right on a hole's cart path (the cart drove round them, the path went through). Every hole's trees now keep off every cart path, and off the tee boxes of other holes - the back and forward tees as well as the main one.

The next tee looks the same from the hole before as it does when you get there: its tee boxes, striped and mown round as they really are; the hole's sign with its card, out to the side where it stands (not a board in the middle of the tee); the tee markers in your colour; the windsock, bench, ball washer and bin; and the cart path beside it.

Golf cart: it no longer drives through trees. It now keeps clear of every tree you can see on the way to the next tee - the woods in the distance and the other holes' trees included, and on the cart path as well as off it - going the long way round if it has to. Where there's no way round, you get the scorecard instead of a ride.

Courses: the green's read comes with the putter wherever you pick it - from the fringe, the fairway or the first cut, the grid and slope shading (with them switched on) now show on the green, lined up from your ball to the hole. And on the fringe they show whatever club you have, so you can read the green before a chip too.

Greens: a new Colours on the grid switch (in the course's and the putting green's options, and the menu) turns the grid's coloured dots plain white while keeping the grid - its lines and the dots rolling downhill still show the slopes, without the colours.

Recording: the scorecard between holes is in the video now, as the game screen shows it - the card after each hole, and on the cart ride the card on the cart's screen with the picture blurred round it. The same in the command centre's box showing the recording.

Swing pad: letting go before you push back up through the ball now plays the shot 10% shorter instead of half a shot or less - and the pad says so plainly: it turns orange with "Let go early - 10% shorter", a phone buzzes three times, and the shot's words start with it.
Swing pad: the ½ (half power) button has moved off the pad, beside its middle on the picture's side and bigger, so a finger starting a swing at the ball no longer catches it.

Replay: with no swing camera - always the case on the phone - Replay (or Q) after a shot on a course now flies that shot again, its tracer drawn as it goes, then brings you back. Where there's nothing to replay, the Replay button isn't offered.

The golf cart keeps out of the very long grass: it no longer drives through it or parks in it by the next tee (it had mistaken it for the next hole's rough), never parks with its wheels in it, and stays out of the waist-high hay most of all.

Graphics: every picture effect now says what it typically costs (heavy, some, light or next to nothing), so you can choose what to turn off first - and, once the speed test has run on your PC, what it measured there.

Android app: the game fills the whole screen, round the camera's hole too, with the swing pad and buttons kept clear of it; and the hole's Replay card sits between the touch strip and the swing pad instead of hidden under the strip.

Android app: the game now loads while you're on the start screen and your route's home - by the time you've picked, it's well on its way - and the house at the top left takes you back to them at any time, with your round or session still there to go back into, nothing loading again. The phone's back button steps back the same way.

Your level now shows what each level hits: on the phone each level's button has its drives (Amateur drives 213-260), and the one picked says how far a full swing drives and a 7 iron carries to start, how far with Power maxed (skill points), and your own with your Power points. On the PC it's under Menu → Mouse and controller → Level.

The cart ride on the PC: with the picture's centre moved over (for hitting down one side of the net), the cart's screen was drawn off to the side and cut off at the edge, the scorecard with it, and scroll bars came up on the window. The screen now comes up in the middle of the picture - the centre goes back where you set it for the next hole - the scorecard always fits the window, and the scroll bars are gone.

Courses: you can putt from off the green if you want to - from the fringe, the fairway or the first cut, go down past the lob wedge to the putter (or say "putter"). It's then played and read as a putt, rolling slower over the grass until it reaches the green, and the read allows for that.
Command centre: between holes, Watch the drive and Next hole are in the heading of the Course box too, so you can go on from the laptop without moving the mouse to the game screen.

Golf cart: you don't have to press Next hole - 40 seconds into the ride the next hole starts by itself, or if the cart is still driving then, once it has been parked by the tee for 5 seconds. The cart's screen counts down the last 10 seconds.

Swing pad and controller: pulling too far or over-swinging now costs much less at the easier levels - hardly anything at Beginner, a little at Amateur, more at Pro and most at Tour - and a pull to 113% still carries close to a full shot (about 88% even at Tour) instead of sometimes only half. The pad gives a little more room past 105% before it counts as too far.

Android app: the game opens much faster - on a slow phone the loading screen goes in about half the time - and a hole you have played before builds in about half the time too, because the phone now keeps each hole once it is built (Menu → Graphics → Holes kept for loading, up to 500 MB).

Android app: lighter graphics made for a phone screen - the effects start on Performance, which on the phone also leaves out the finest grass, sand grains and wet-ground shine; shadows, leaf pictures and textures are smaller; trees switch to their simpler versions sooner; and the picture is drawn at most 60 times a second, even on a 90 or 120 Hz screen. It looks much the same at phone size, with less heat, battery and memory used.
The game starts a little faster after the first time: the trees are kept with the holes kept for loading rather than made again at every start.

The cart between holes now waits on flat short grass by the green and stops on the flat by the next tee - no more parking in a bunker or on a slant - and drives round trees (well clear of their branches), sand, water, greens and tee boxes on every hole, keeping out of very long grass and off steep banks unless there's no other way.

Chipping on the touch screen (or with the mouse): the new ½ button on the swing pad makes its gold line a 50% swing, so every percent takes twice the pull - a short chip gets a line long enough to draw to. Press ½ again for full power.

Seasons now start against golfers at your own level: the field is drawn round your handicap. If you haven't played enough rounds to have one yet, the Season panel asks for yours and plays off it until your rounds give you one - for the launch monitor and for mouse, touch or controller play separately.

In a season event two of the field play with you: a box over the picture shows everyone's strokes on the hole you're on (friends' too, in any round with others), and the leaderboard so far shows on the scorecard between holes and on the cart's screen.

The phone app now keeps your stats: every shot and round you play on it, at the range with a launch monitor or on the swing pad. At the range, Send to your PC puts them into your PC's My stats - press Get the phone's stats there and type the code it shows on the phone. They go in at the times you hit them, and sending again only sends what's new.
Your handicaps come back to the phone with each send - the launch monitor's, and the swing pad's and a controller's at each level, each kept apart - and the phone plays off them on its courses.

Skill points for the swing pad and controllers: rounds and challenges played with them earn XP, and XP earns points to spend on eleven skills - Power, Accuracy, Curve control, Consistency, Feel, Tempo, Strike, Trajectory, Short game, Putting and Recovery. 75 points at most, and past 60 they're far harder to earn, so pick what you want to be good at (Menu, Swing pad & controller, Skill points). Moving points is free below level 5, then once a season.

A shot set up before you swing - higher, lower, more spin, a draw or a fade - is now harder to hit: a crooked swing goes more crooked and the window round the flag's mark is narrower. A stock shot plays as before, the shot setup card says the price, and the Trajectory skill takes back what a height or spin adds.

Swing pad and controller distances now depend on your level: a good drive (carry and roll) goes 180 yards at Beginner, 213 at Amateur, 245 at Pro and 262 at Tour, and Power skill points take it up to 220, 260, 300 and 320 - every club with it (a long hitter's irons a little less: a Tour player's 7 iron carries about 180), and the club suggested fits. Custom picks which level's distances it plays.

A new swing pad or controller player's handicap now starts as the golfer their level is named after - Beginner 28, Amateur 15, Pro 5, Tour scratch - so a Tour player gives a Beginner strokes. After three rounds your own scores take over.
Online, the host can play with each player's skill points or none (Skill points online, on the course panel).

Phone app: the screen while you play is much less busy. The words over the picture sit between the touch buttons and the swing pad, a short line each (the hole, what the lie does to your carry, the slope), and the numbers along the bottom stay clear of the swing pad, so the lie and the rest are always readable. The whole sentences are in the side panel.
Phone app: the swing pad stands clear of the side panel's tab, so the tab is easy to open, and no keyboard keys are mentioned - the card before a round just says Start a round.
Phone app: the frame rate, if you show it, is just the number at the top of the picture. Tap it to see the rest.

Phone app: before a round, each course that comes with the app plays a flyover film of its first hole straight away, while the hole itself gets ready behind it. A course of your own shows a flyover of another hole until its own is ready.

Beside a bunker with a raised lip, the fairway now runs cleanly up to the sand: the dark, saw-toothed patches that showed on the fairway next to some bunkers (Golf Sim Links' 2nd among them) are gone.

Mouse and controller swings now have set club distances: a full swing (100%) carries each club its own distance - the driver 230 yds, a 7 iron 150 - and a 90% swing 90% of it, down to a little chip with a wedge. As you pull back, the swing pad shows the swing's size and how far it carries (or a putt's feet).

You can overswing, but only to 105%: a little further, and every percent past 100 makes a crooked swing more crooked and the shot less predictable. On a controller a full swing is just short of the stick's edge and 105% is right at it, with a tap of rumble at each (Controller rumble in the menu turns it off).

The swing's rhythm counts too: pull back about three times as long as you push through for a smooth swing - rushed or snatched, the shot comes out shorter and more crooked. What the shot did says its size, its line and its rhythm.

Shot setup: before a full shot or a chip, press Y on the controller (or Shot on the swing pad) to curve it left or right, hit it lower (a punch, or a bump and run near the green) or higher (a flop with a wedge), and put more or less spin on it. A curving shot still lands where you aim. It lasts the one shot.

Levels for the mouse and the controller: Beginner (a mark on the pad where to stop for the flag, close enough counts, putts read for you), Amateur, Pro (your own distances and reads) and Tour (every fault shows), or Custom with each help a switch. Each saved player can have their own (Saved players); the old How forgiving setting carries over.

Controller and mouse players now get a handicap of their own for each level, kept apart from their real one, so they can play fairly against someone on a launch monitor: in a round each player plays off the handicap for how they're swinging, and the round card says which. Until you've played three rounds at a level it starts from that level's own figure.

Online, the host's mouse and controller rule now sets the easiest level anyone may swing at (Amateur, Pro or Tour), and Y on the controller is now the shot setup - the camera's follow / stay put is on the controller panel (View).

Calibration is gone: the flight is close to the launch monitor's own carries without any setting up, so the calibration panel (Shift + C), its page, Calibrate in Shot history and saying "calibrate" have all been taken out.
Carry adjustment (Menu, Ball flight) is still there if you want every club a little further or shorter: 0 is A² Golf's own flight.

Online, everyone sees each bay's carry adjustment: beside the bay in Online play, when the game starts, and if it's changed during the game. The host can have everyone play A² Golf's own carries instead (Carry adjustments online, in the course panel); each bay's adjustment comes back when the game ends.
Bunkers with a raised far face no longer show a dark crack or a thin line of sky along the top of the face.

Ponds: the bright green line along the top of a pond's bank is gone. The grass now runs down the bank towards the water - nearly to it on gentle stretches, over pale silt and gravel, and stopping at a short worn bank of earth on steeper ones - so each stretch of shore looks different, and the water is muddy and shallow where it meets the bank.
Bunker edges vary: some cut clean with a thin dark line of soil, some with the grass thinning softly into the sand, some ragged and worn - a mix on parkland courses, mostly clean-cut on modern ones.

The mown grass flows as a mower leaves it: no thin strips of rough left between the fairway and the grass round the green, the first cut goes on round the ends of the fairway, and tee boxes close together share one mown surround.
Hay: waist-high grass gone to seed, past a links hole's long grass where a ball would be lost, and in drifts by the trees on some parkland holes. It plays as deep rough.

Links burns now run in a channel of their own below the grass, the fairway mown right down their banks to the water, instead of a flat ribbon of water lying on the grass - and you can change one in the hole editor just like a brook.

Brooks and burns have banks worn by their water: a short face of earth under a ragged lip of turf on the outside of a bend, a narrow muddy margin with the grass nearly to the water elsewhere. They stop short of any bunker beside them.

Brooks and burns lie deeper, in a proper channel with steeper banks: from the fairway you see the far bank's face, lit by the sun or in shade, and the water shows the sky along the near side and the far bank mirrored along the far side - no longer a flat dark green stripe.
Water seen low from close by keeps its soft sheen of the sky instead of going very dark; a pond seen almost edge on from the tee still reads as dark water.
The hay has seed heads now - spikes and nodding plumes - close to and far off.

The long grass round you looks fuller: each tuft grows out of the ground in the ground's own colour with no dark foot, the tufts spread a little wider close to the camera, and the ground between them is a bolder grass.
