Every tree's leaves fall in patches of light and shade of its own, so two trees of the same shape side by side no longer look like the same tree.
On courses made from a map, thin strips and corners of rough left between a fairway, a tee and a green are mown, as a mower leaves them.

Behind the scenes: the ground round a hole's bunkers, and the mower's line, are worked out quicker and a part at a time while the next hole is made ready, for fewer hitches. Nothing should play differently.

Behind the scenes: the first steps towards an Android version - a test app that plays the game on a phone with no PC, on the touch screen or with the Omni over the phone's Bluetooth. Nothing should play differently.

The side panel folds away: the tab on the picture's right edge hides it and brings it back, and it folds by itself when you hit a shot or start a round, so the picture has the whole width - the shot's numbers along the bottom of the picture instead. The pin under the tab keeps it open while you play (also Menu, Screens, Side panel pinned open).

Playing with a finger on a phone or tablet: a strip on the other side of the picture from the swing pad has the club (a longer or shorter one), the aim (tap or hold the arrows, or draw a finger sideways across the picture) and buttons for what's useful just then - Read and New putt on the green, Ball view in the trees, Next hole, Skip a flyover, Replay - with More for everything else. On a phone the top bar keeps to one row and the swing pad no longer covers the menu.

Mouse, finger and controller swings are no longer the same every time: even a perfect swing now has a golfer's own spread - a few yards longer or shorter, a little left or right, and now and then one off the middle that comes up well short. Least at Beginner, most at Tour. Putts vary a little too.
The swing pad shows its lines before you touch it - where to stop for the flag, a full swing and the most - with what the flag's swing carries, so you can see the swing to make before you start it.
The strike feels immediate: the pad flashes as you strike, and on a phone it gives a short buzz as the pull reaches 100% and 105%, and as it strikes.

Quicker between shots, most of all on a phone: the ball goes the moment you strike, coming onto a green no longer stops or slows the picture while the putt is read, and played with a finger the side panel starts folded away.
The game no longer assumes you have a Square Omni: the loading screen, the welcome, the tips and the phone's choices talk about your launch monitor.

The swing pad draws the way your finger (or mouse) went - the pull down and the push back up through the ball - so when you push across the line to hook or slice it, you see the curve you drew. The bar stays at the swing's size while you push.
Pulling far past 105% now hurts: the pad goes red and says Too far!, and the shot is over the top - shorter, sprayed off line, and often badly mishit. A touch past 105% is let go.

The phone app now opens on a choice of two: Play (golf with your finger - a round, the range and greens, the challenges, your level) or At the range (with your launch monitor - a range session or a course). The one you used last comes first, and Menu, Change route goes back to it. The phone's menu leaves out what's only for a PC bay.
Smoother on a phone: the phone app draws the 3D picture at far fewer pixels - about a third as many on Medium - and stretches it to fill the screen, with the words and buttons still sharp.
The frame rate's line (Show the frame rate) now says the picture's size in pixels as well.
The loading screen's picture of a course's tee shows the tee again, not a dark screen.

Play with friends on the phone app: from Play, host a game and give your friends its code, or type theirs to join - phones and PC bays play the same round together, each hitting their own shots. The phone plays online by code only (no home network or Tailscale).

The first cut now runs right up to the long grass. Where it curves round to meet the mown grass by the green, and beside the ends of the fairway, a dark wedge of bare ground used to show between them.

A new look for the menus and buttons. The menu's pages are sorted by subject in three groups - Play (Play, Players, Swing pad & controller, Ball flight, Greens), Set up (Launch monitor, Screens, Graphics, Cameras & video, Sound & voice) and More (Stats, Help, System) - and each setting says what it does in two lines, with More for the rest.

On the phone the menu is a page at a time: a list of big tiles, tap one, and Menu at the top goes back - every switch and button big enough for a thumb. The top bar is a few big buttons: where you are (tap it for the five places to play), the club, who's hitting, sound and Menu.
Prefer the old look? Menu, Screens, Menus and buttons: Legacy puts the menus and buttons back as they were, and New brings this one back.

Island greens can now be made on a par 3: a pond grown right round the green is no longer stopped by the cart path beside it - where the path meets the water it crosses on a timber bridge (or ends on a little jetty).

Course designer: Play this hole plays just that hole, then shows its scorecard and takes you back to the designer on the same hole - it no longer carries on round the rest of the course, and it isn't kept as a round.
Hole editor: change a pond's shape - pick it and drag the blue marks round its edge to push the shore out or pull it in, with the edge running smoothly between them. Its own shape again puts it back.

Hole editor: the Fairway tool's new Add and move puts more fairway on a hole - tap anywhere (in front of a par 3's green, behind it, out to one side), then drag it, size it with its white dot or shape it with the blue marks round its edge. It plays as fairway with its first cut round it, and the hole's own trees are cleared off it.

An island green's causeway now runs onto a fairway if there's one near - so with the whole front of a par 3 under water and a fairway behind the green, the walk off goes out the back onto that fairway.

Hole editor: water can now be as big as a lake needs and come right up to the tee box, and the causeway to an island green reaches however far the land is. When a pond can't go somewhere, the red outline now says why (on the tee, off this hole's ground, as big as it goes).

Hole editor: shape an island green's causeway with the Fairway tool's new Causeway - make it wider (up to 30 m), flare its ends out where they meet the green and the land, or drag the yellow dot at its end to turn it round the green and run it further onto the land.

Voice no longer puts a "did you say this?" box over the game, in any mode. When it hears something other than a club, it says what it heard in the messages - say "confirm" or press Y to do it, or just carry on and nothing happens.

Menu, Screens: the new WebGPU test flies the same 20 seconds round the driving range drawn three ways - today's WebGL and the new WebGPU renderer on WebGL 2 and on WebGPU - and shows each one's frames a second with a picture of it, to see what WebGPU would do on your PC. Send to Claude passes the results on. (The new renderer draws nearly all of the range as the game does now - the grass, sand, water, sky, haze, clouds, nets, far woods, the tufts in the rough, the trees and plants swaying in the wind with the sun coming through their leaves, the bark, flags, rocks, cart paths, the water's sparkle, the rain and the balls' shine; only the sand and spray a ball throws up is still to come.)

Between holes, a cart ride to the next tee: a cart waits by the green, the camera gets in and looks up at the screen under its roof - the scorecard on it, the course blurred round it - while it drives to the next tee and the next hole finishes loading. Next hole once it is ready, or Watch the drive to follow the cart to the tee first. (Menu, Play: Ride the cart to the next tee - off, the scorecard over the picture as before.)

On High and Ultra graphics the cart between holes is now a proper golf cart: a rounded cream body with headlamps, tail lamps and a pinstripe, tyres with tread on silver spoked wheels, padded seats with grab rails, a steering wheel and dash, an arched canopy over a clear windscreen, and the bags with their headcovers and irons on the back. Standard and Medium keep the simpler cart.

Three screens: the command centre opens straight away as A² Golf starts, beside the game and the shot data, showing the loading card until its controls come in - as soon as the game has made them, while the picture's still getting ready.

Island greens: a green with water all round now gets a strip of fairway across to the nearest land, built by itself. It plays as fairway, the water stops at its edges, and it's there for as long as the green's an island - move the pond or the green to the shore and it goes.

Island greens: no tree, bush or decoration stands on the strip of fairway out to the green, or right beside it - any that was there goes while the green's an island, and the hole editor won't plant one there.

Trees take about 28 MB less memory on Ultra (about 23 MB on High), and if the graphics card ever resets the picture, the far tree line comes back with it - before, it stayed empty for the rest of the game. A hole from a map gets ready a little quicker as the one before it is played.

Trees: no more large gaps where the sky shows through a crown, and no leaves hanging in the air off it - the crown fills out its leaves, near and close up, on tall trees too. Close up, a tree's branches are plainer, hidden in its fuller crown (a birch keeps its twigs).
Trees: a birch's leaves now have branches to them further off too, not only close up - a plain branch from its trunk into each clump of leaves.
Smoother play on parkland courses: the glimpses of the course's other holes are now built in small steps while the next hole gets ready, so they no longer cause a brief pause.

Trees close up: each leaf has its side veins and lays a soft shadow on the leaves under it, with the lightest on top, so a crown looks layered rather than flat. The far tree line is as full as the trees in front of it, and the leaves take about 34 MB less memory on Ultra.
Setup steps, connection messages and the guide no longer name other golf software: where it matters, they just say to close any other program connected to your launch monitor.
Command centre: when the mode's buttons don't fit on one row (putting's tabs and cup buttons on a smaller window), the mode's box gives them two rows instead of hiding the first under the top bar.

Command centre, arranging (Shift + B): the boxes in the mode's box can now be dragged anywhere inside it and sized by their edges, and stay where you put them - the rest fit round them. Tidy up packs them again.

Command centre, arranging: the big Arrange panel minimises to a small strip (its Minimise button, or H) so it's out of the way of the boxes you're moving - Show the panel brings it back, and it stays as you left it.

Problem reports: when the same problem happens again, the update to its report now says what was going on that time too (how long the game had been running, the memory, the recording and the graphics), so it can be tracked down without sending a report by hand.

Recording: if the graphics card crashes while you record, the video now holds the game's last picture with "The game's picture is coming back..." instead of carrying on with the game missing, and if the picture doesn't come back by itself the game reopens to get it back, the recording carrying on in its next file.
Command centre: the Messages box stays in its drawer tab when a message or card comes in - a number on the tab says how many are new, and goes when you open it.
Fewer messages: aiming, stepping along the putt's line, a flat green and changing club or mode no longer each leave a message - what changed is on the screen already.

The view behind the ball is lower and closer, like a golfer standing behind it - no longer like looking down from somewhere tall - with a lens closer to your own eye's, so the hole ahead looks bigger. The range's view from the tee is the same.

The mini map and the course designer show brown links holes as brown dunes - khaki rough, straw long grass, a yellower fairway, with the sandy and heather patches - as they look in the game, not all green.
Recordings get 10 GB of disk to begin with (it was 5) - about two hours at 1080p60 - with the oldest still deleted first to make room. A size you've set yourself stays as it is.

Three screens: the projector (or any screen) not yet on as the game starts no longer loses its window for good - the window waits elsewhere and goes back when the screen comes on, the shot data included - and the controls window gets longer to open while the game loads, so three screens don't come back as two.
Who's playing opens on the command centre screen at start-up, waiting for it to open, rather than on the projector.

A new video, the Launch trailer (Menu, Play, Videos): A² Golf in about four minutes for YouTube - friends online, designing your own course, practising and getting better, the weather and an ace. Every video's recording now has a cue sheet beside it, and a tool that comes with the code lays your music under the trailer, adds YouTube chapters and cuts four upright Shorts from it.

Trees are cheaper to draw and to hold, and look just as they did: each leaf card is trimmed to the leaves on it, so the busiest woods take about a fifth less drawing, and all the trees on the course now share one copy of the tree shapes - about 45 MB less memory on Ultra once the next hole is built (and as much less graphics memory), with 20 MB less graphics memory for the far woods' pictures.

Reflections in ponds on Ultra are a little cheaper on a calm day: only what the ripples could actually bend into view is drawn for them, by how rough the water is just now, rather than as much as the roughest water ever needs. In a gale with rain the reflection no longer misses the odd speck at its edge.

Bunkers and water react to the ball: sand puffs up where a ball lands in a bunker, and a bunker shot blasts a fan of sand out ahead of it with a haze of dust - more from a ball plugged in the sand. A ball going into water throws up a splash of drops and white water, and if it goes in close to the edge it splashes the bank dark for a while. On Ultra the ball also leaves its marks in the sand: a dent where it lands, the scoop a bunker shot takes, and the crater round a plugged ball. On Medium and up, on the course and the range.

New courses have more natural bunkers and water: now and then a greenside bunker curves round the green, bunkers come in a wider spread of sizes - small ones, big ones and long ones down the edge of a fairway - and some have a flashed face, the sand climbing the far side to a raised lip of grass you can see from the fairway (a ball on it runs back down into the bunker). Some ponds off the side of a hole are natural lakes, and a lake's far shore can be a wetland of wide, muddy shallows thick with reeds. The ready-made courses are given again with them; any you've changed is kept too, as "your copy". Courses you made before stay as they were.
Two bunkers that overlap are one patch of sand again, dug once: no grass edge across the sand between them, and the sand where they meet no deeper than either.

The green always comes first: a pond or lake that runs onto a green - a course made from a map could draw one right across it - now stops at the edge of the green's fringe, with its muddy shore there, and the green and fringe play, putt and look as they should. A pond's bank no longer digs into a green beside it either. Water that stops short of a green, like a pond walled up to it, is just as it was.
In the hole editor a pond can now go over a green, or all the way round it for an island green (a brook or a pond with a wall still can't reach the green).

No more short pauses while the next hole is got ready in the background: on a links hole with deep pot bunkers the longest was nearly two seconds, and now each piece of the work takes under a fifth of a second. The holes come out exactly as before.

Blind shots on courses on hills have an aiming post: where you can't see where your drive will land from the tee, a tall red and cream post stands on top of the rise that hides it, on the line to the landing - aim over it. A par 3 whose flag you can't see from the tee has one too, and the Alps hole has one on its ridge, on the line to the flag. Every course on hills gets them, those you made before too.

Online golf pong in turn: when two players at the same bay putt one after the other, the other bays now see both putts roll, one after the other. The second used to be left out there - its cup just disappeared. In four-way, a putt at a cup round to the side of the rack beside you counts now: the host used to turn it down, and the bay that putted it showed the cup holed, then quietly put it back.
Online play by code: if the host turns down something your bay sent, you're told on the screen, as you are playing across the house - and golf pong goes back to how the host has the game.

The Omni no longer flicks between connected and "looking for the Omni" in the top bar after the game has been left a while without it: a second, hidden connection to it was left open that kept saying it was still starting.

The frame rate box (Shift + F) counts the picture's own triangles, so the number holds steady instead of jumping each time the shadows are drawn again. While they keep being drawn again it says how often, and a report says what made them.
The Omni's "Marking ball" tick is gone from the menu: the Omni measures spin on any ball, so it's no longer a choice, and every shot is read just as before. The Launch monitor page now says so.

No more long freezes while the game gets holes ready in the background: on courses made from a map (Hillside Park, Nine Oaks Mountain) the long grass is worked out about ten times quicker on Ultra, and never in one go - one report showed the game frozen for nearly two minutes. Links holes get ready quicker too.
The speed test no longer freezes for several seconds while it gets each setting ready.

Ultra is smoother while the camera flies: following a ball through the air, flyovers and the look down the hole are drawn at your screen's own sharpness, and the extra sharpness comes back the moment the camera stops. Recordings keep theirs all the way through.

The game no longer takes more memory with every hole you play: each hole's trees, long grass and Ultra's grass across the hole are let go of with it (on Ultra that was about 30 MB a hole). And after watching the last hole again with J, its trees change from far to near as the camera comes close again.

The dunes on a links course look like dunes from the air: their ridges wind and branch, where before they ran in straight lines and right angles that showed as terraces from a high camera. A ball in the dunes still kicks off the ridges and runs into the hollows.

A links hole full of pot bunkers is quicker to draw: the finely shaped ground round each pot now covers just the pot and its banks, not 80 metres round it hidden under the rest of the ground. Nothing looks or plays any differently.
Where the next tee is right beside the green you've just played, there's no longer a board for it standing there: you can see the tee.

On a links course the only sand is in the bunkers, on and beside the fairways and by the greens: the patches of bare sand out in the dunes, which played and looked like bunkers in odd places, are gone.

Following a ball through the air on Ultra is smoother, most on a links course: from up in the air the grass across the hole isn't drawn as far out (it fills in as the camera comes down to where the ball lands, where it's already grown), and reflections in the sea and in ponds are drawn every other frame while the camera glides, which halves what they cost. The grass a shot grows no longer shows up in the water for a moment as each shot is set up.

Recordings on Ultra are sharp again: the picture is supersampled while recording, as far as the recording can use - a 1280 x 800 game screen is drawn 1,080 lines tall for a 1080p recording - instead of not at all. If the picture can't keep up while recording, that's the first thing eased.
Making a course is quicker: laying it out on hills, routing its holes and finding the best holes (Best holes) all take less time, and the courses come out exactly as they did before.

Tidy up in the command centre no longer makes the game box so wide that the other boxes go off the bottom of the screen: it leaves room for them all beside it. A box in the game box that doesn't fit is made shorter rather than pushed out of sight.

On Golf Sim Links the 18th tee is no longer right beside the 17th green: the 17th now swings a little further round, so you walk off the green to a tee that's clear of it. Nine Oaks Mountain's 9th tee is off the 8th green too, and new courses you make keep each next tee a short walk from the green you've just played, not on top of it. (The ready-made courses are given again for this; any you've changed is kept as well, as "your copy".)

Trees look fuller and rounder: broad-leaved trees have more, finer leaves, and each crown is lit as one rounded mass in the sun rather than as a bunch of separate balls. They're cheaper to draw too - about a third fewer triangles a tree, every kind's leaves drawn together, and the branches of the trees close to you lighter - so a hole lined with trees runs a little smoother, most on High and Ultra.

Bunkers and ponds sit in the ground now instead of lying flat on it. Every bunker on a designed course is dug a little below the grass, deeper by the green, with a face from its rim down to the sand - so there's a small lip to clear (nearly any club with a little loft gets out). Ponds lie a foot or so below the grass, the grass rolling over the edge onto a bank of earth that runs down into the water. Pot bunkers, waste areas and courses from a map are as they were.

Reflections in ponds on Ultra are cheaper: only what could actually be seen in a pond from where you are is drawn for it, rather than the whole hole again - a quarter to a third less from up in the air as you follow a ball. What the pond shows is exactly the same.

More kinds of tree shape: every kind of tree now comes in two more shapes, each with a look of its own - pines grown tall in a wood with a small crown high on a long trunk, and young ones full to the ground; broad-leaved trees grown out from the edge of a wood, and parkland plane trees with a broad dome on a tall, clear trunk; weeping and broad old birches, willows leaning far over, slender and fuller poplars, young and forked Scots pines, upright and storm-bent oaks, slim cypresses and broad old yews, old spruces with their lower branches sweeping the ground, broken stumps and dead trees with bare branches only at the top. About one tree in four takes one of them; the rest keep the shape they had. A tree plays exactly as it looks, whichever shape it is, and in the hole editor you can give trees any of their kind's shapes.

Trees close to you have finer branches: on High and Ultra a broad-leaved tree's limbs branch on into twigs out to its leaves, with some of the leaves in sprays on the twigs, so the edge of the crown breaks up and you can see the branches through it from underneath. Plane trees have their own broad, five-pointed leaves, and each part of a tree's crown is its own shade of green, a little warmer or cooler than the next.

The signs for the next hole no longer stand beside the green you've just played: the arrow on to the next tee now stands on the way there, at least 15 metres from the green, pointing at the tee, and the next tee's board is moved on past the tee to 15 metres from the green where the tee itself is closer than that.

No more trees standing right in front of the next hole's tee: the trees round a green were often planted in the next tee's view down to its fairway. Every hole's tee shot now has a clear view, as it always had of its own trees.
Links holes no longer have sand scrapes out on the beach: they stay in the hole's own dunes.
A burn across a links fairway now shows its water: it was drawn murky green from bank to bank, and from above looked like a dark streak across the fairway.
On courses on hills, another hole's fairway running past the back of the hole no longer has a dark strip of rough across it where the hole's ground ends.

Recordings are about half the size: a new Format setting in the Recording panel (Recording and sound) records in H.265 where your graphics card can - much the same picture in a little over half the space, about 3 GB an hour at 1080p 60 on Best instead of 5.5. Windows' own Media Player needs Microsoft's HEVC Video Extensions to play these (VLC, YouTube, phones and the game play them as they are); choose Plays anywhere (H.264) for files every player opens.
Recordings also look a little better for their size: a whole picture every 4 seconds instead of every couple of seconds, with the frames between only what changed.

Every replay you have saved is now in one place: Menu, Cameras & video, Every saved replay (or Every saved replay... in the Cameras panel, or the Saved replays page in the Recording panel). Each saved shot is listed newest first with who hit it, the club and the carry; Watch plays all its camera angles side by side from the swing, in slow motion if you like, and Delete removes a shot you no longer want.

The sky is a clear blue again when the sun is high: it no longer washes out to a pale grey-blue at midday, the higher the sun the deeper the blue overhead, and the glow round the sun is smaller. The clouds stand out whiter against it. A sky at dusk looks as it did.

Every edge a mower makes is now a neat line: the fairway, the first cut, the tees and the greens. The long grass stands up in a straight, unbroken line right along each cut, with no blades straggling over it - only the deep rough and the grass round bunkers, water, paths and trees keep their natural edges. Every tee box has a strip of first cut round it and every green a channel of first cut past its fringe; these play as first cut and show on the hole map.

A crash no longer ends a recording: when the game opens again after a crash, the recording carries on by itself in a new file, kept with the rest of it, and says about how much is missing. The file that was cut off is saved as it was. Closing or reloading the game on purpose still ends the recording there and then.

On Ultra the blades of grass on the fairway and the tee now follow the mowing stripes: on a dark stripe they're dark, on a light one light, so the stripes run on through the grass instead of the blades showing up pale across the dark stripes. The tee's grass is the tee's own colour too.
A new setting, Celebration effects (Menu, Screens, The picture): switch it off for no confetti, streamers or fireworks - just the score and the crowd cheering, with no other sounds.

A birdie, an eagle and a hole in one now get a real crowd round the green instead of a made-up fanfare: applause for a birdie, a cheer for an eagle, and the whole gallery roaring for a hole in one or an albatross. A different recording each time; the made-up fanfares come back if you turn recordings off in the Sound panel.

The celebrations look new too: confetti cannons either side of the flag fire confetti and paper streamers up over it, gold and silver foil flashes among the confetti, and the fireworks come in four kinds - a ball of sparks, a ring, a gold willow and crackling glitter. A birdie's confetti comes from the cannons one time and rains from the sky the next.

The command centre's side drawer now comes over the boxes instead of pushing them across: opening it moves nothing, and closing it shows the boxes underneath again. It starts closed; click a drawer tab to open it and click the same tab again to close it.

While arranging the command centre you can minimise the drawer (D, or its button) to lay out the boxes under it, then open it to drop boxes in and minimise it again. Dropping a box on one of its tabs on the edge puts it in that tab, and dropping one on + tab starts a new tab with it.

Boxes in the drawer can be sized now: while arranging, drag a box's bottom edge to make it taller or shorter, use − and + for its text, and drag the drawer's left edge to make it wider - each tab keeps its own width. A box on a tab of its own (the Options or the Keys, say) fills the whole drawer.

Fixed: a shot the launch monitor sent twice could be played twice - the ball moved to where the first one landed and the same shot went again from there. A shot that comes in twice is now only ever played once.

Mulligans: switch them on in the course's Options (or Menu, Play, The round) and Shift + M takes your last stroke back - in the air or after it's stopped - so you can play it again from where you were. Never in online play or a scramble, and off to begin with.

The crowd gets more excited the better the score: a birdie gets a round of applause, an eagle two cheers from either side of the green and louder, and a hole in one the whole gallery roaring - loudest of all.

The command centre is now the same screen whatever you're playing. This shot, the messages, the game screen and the rest stay where you put them, and each mode's own boxes - the scorecard, the map, the dispersion - go in one box, the mode's box, that stays in the same place and just changes what's in it when you change mode. Move and size it as one while arranging.

A second drawer down the left of the command centre holds the options for the mode you're in: Practice on the range, This putt on the putting green, the course, season and round options on the course, and so on. Open it from its tab on the left edge (A while arranging); the keys and the shot history stay in the drawer on the right. Any box can go in either drawer.

While arranging the command centre, every box now says whose it is - All modes in blue, or Course only (Putting only...) in green - and See each mode on the arrange bar shows how the window looks in each mode without the game going there, so you can check they all fit. Boxes for every mode, the top bar included, now never move unless you move them.

Golf Sim Links, Sea Links and Hillside Park are made again the way the course designer now makes a new course with Best holes: other designs of each weak hole tried and the best course kept - new designs of five of Golf Sim Links' holes and five of Hillside Park's - and the stroke indexes set from how the holes play. Your copies are replaced as the game starts; one you've changed is kept as your copy.

The game's videos are played on these new courses: every hole still the one picked for what it shows, and every shot found again on it. The Looks and sound video now shows the picture effects from behind the tee of Hillside Park's 9th, its lake right across the line in front.
Fixed: a course made on hills with Best holes on had its holes laid out as on flat ground. They're routed over the hills again, finding the land, as with Best holes off.

The command centre has a new This shot box for every mode, in place of the Shot details and each mode's own result, guide, lie, target and status boxes: who's hitting and with what (and the club the game suggests if you've picked another), the result and the note in full, the lie and putt guidance, the lie of the land drawn as on the game screen, the distance to the pin and the score - and Next shot buttons (Normal, Punch / low, Part swing, Something else, or a power from 25% to Full) to click instead of pressing E.

A Last shot box shows the last shot's numbers for every mode: the range's carry, total, launch and spin, the putt's ball speed, start line, the pace it needed and how far it finished, the chip's carry, landing, leave and roll - and on the course and in the Challenges the launch monitor's numbers with the flight the ball really flew.

Each mode's tabs and play buttons - Practice, Distance challenge, Golf pong, Start round, Start, Pick a game, New game, the putt's aim, Session view - are now along the top of the mode's box in the command centre, so they're never shut away in a closed drawer. The mode's boxes are drawn bigger when there's room, so the box isn't half empty.

Cards that want an answer (Odd shot?, the graphics question, the course's card before a round and the rest) now sit at the top of the Messages box in the command centre until they're answered, instead of sliding out of the drawer.

The Game screen box has Replay and Save for the last shot's replay on its heading; the club picker is in the top bar on the course and in the Challenges too; the shot history can mark a shot Something else; and golf pong's score has a box of its own.

Fixed: the flight path on recordings and in the command centre's flight boxes was the launch monitor's numbers flown again in still air, not the shot you saw. It's now the flight the game really flew - its wind, the lie, the air and, on a course, the ground it came down on - with that flight's carry, total, apex, hang time and descent.

The command centre's top bar now shows the laptop's time, so you can see it at a glance without reaching for your phone (the date is in its tooltip). For a bigger one, add a Clock box from the Arrange bar.

Trees no longer bleed light. Sunlight through the leaves is now a subtle glow only where the sun really reaches a leaf - along a crown's edge, on a leaf out on its own - never across a whole crown or one standing in another tree's shade, and the underside of a crown is no longer lit up from within.

Fixed the white blobs (sometimes red) that flashed on the screen: the sun's reflection in the ball and on ponds was far too bright for the bloom, which spread it into a hard white disc, and the sun itself could get into the bloom through the gaps in a swaying tree. Glints now bloom softly, the sky never does, and the picture's effects no longer pass on a bad pixel.

Trees read as rounded now, near and far: every crown is shaded darker in its heart and underneath and lightest outside and on top, as only the close-up trees were, so a tree is a round mass with light and shade in it rather than a flat green clump.

A new picture effect, Harder sunlight, on to begin with: a stronger sun and a softer light from the sky, as on a clear day, so shade is under a third as bright as the sun rather than half, and trees, slopes and bunker faces stand out - less so as the sun gets low, so an evening round isn't dark. Switch it off under Picture effects for the softer light the game had.

The far woods are lit by the sun from the side it's on (Medium and up): each far tree's picture now knows which way it faces, so the distant tree line has light and shade across it instead of being one flat band, and the trees across a hole keep their lit side towards the sun as you move round them.

On the range the ball now sits on the right-hand side of the hitting mat for a right-hander, with room for your feet on the left, and on the left-hand side for a left-hander (each player's hand is in Players); the pyramid of balls stands on the other side. The mats change round as a left-hander steps up.

Ball flight: low-spin drives now fly the way the Omni and other simulators fly them - higher and further through the air, landing a little steeper and rolling out less - instead of flying low and short and then running on a long way. A 1500 rpm drive at 150 mph that used to carry 219 yards and roll 45 now carries about 237 and rolls about 34. Totals stay much the same; it is the split between carry and roll that has changed. Your lowest-spin Omni drives now carry within 1-3% of what the Omni shows.

Every drive flies a truer shape too: a tour-speed drive now peaks about 34 yards high and lands at 38 degrees, as on TrackMan, and spin fades through the flight at the rate measured in the wind tunnel. Higher launch with less spin carries further, as on the Omni - but a drive with next to no spin from a normal launch still falls out of the sky.

The ground was set again to go with it: on a normal fairway a drive still runs out 15-25 yards (a low-spin one about 30), firm ground about half as far again, soft ground and the first cut about half, the rough about a third - and a well-struck wedge still spins back on soft ground.

If you had matched A-Squared Golf to your Omni on the calibration page, that match is set aside with the new flight (it was made for the old one) - you should not need it now, but you can fit one again from fresh shots. Your older shots in My stats are brought into line with the new flight automatically.

Other launch monitors can play: choose yours in the menu (Launch monitor) or on the welcome screen, and the steps to set it up show underneath, with this PC's address and the port already filled in. Garmin R10, Rapsodo MLM2PRO, Uneekor, SkyTrak, Foresight GC2, ES16, PiTrac and anything else that talks to GSPro - plus Mevo+, R50, TrackMan, Full Swing KIT and SC4 through a community program that reads their app. The Square Omni still connects by itself over Bluetooth, as before.
A Garmin R10 needs no extra program: in the Garmin Golf app, connect E6 Connect to this PC's address and A² Golf plays each shot and gets the R10 ready for the next one.

The top bar waits for your launch monitor by name (Waiting for your Garmin Approach R10) and names it once it's connected (Garmin Approach R10 connected), and a radar's spin, which it works out rather than measures, is kept out of your spin tips.

Fixed for launch monitors that send their shots through a connector: Uneekor's shots no longer fly with no spin, shots some connectors mark oddly are no longer missed, club data sent after its shot is kept with it, and a shot a connector sends twice is played once. Connectors that wait to be told the game is ready for the next shot (the SkyTrak's, the community Square one) are now told.

Twice as much long grass on the course, and cheaper to draw: only the tufts within a dozen metres or so of you are drawn in full, every one further off as a single cheap card of blades that keeps its colour at any distance. From the air the grass and the ground between the tufts are one colour now - the long grass round the ball no longer shows as a darker ring, and the rough right under a high camera reads as standing grass rather than a flat carpet.
The course's other holes are no longer cut off beside the hole you're playing: from the air a neighbouring fairway, green and tee run on whole, bunkers and all, through your hole's rough.
In the rain the rough no longer shines like the fairway, so trees along a hole don't look as if they're standing on a fairway.

Any box in the command centre can go in its side drawer: drag it onto the drawer (it opens while you arrange), press its → drawer, or use Arrange ▾ (← out takes one back out). The drawer has tabs too: + for another, ✎ to name it, and drop a box on a tab's name to put it there.

The command centre stays put: each box keeps its place instead of the whole screen rearranging itself when the ball reaches the green or a box comes or goes. Boxes are only packed again to make room, or when you open or close the drawer.

No more pop-ups after a shot asking about it. A club that flew like another, a very short shot, a thin or fat strike on the range, a reading that didn't look right, a chip that went like another swing and the end of a session each just leave a message in the Messages box, saying what was kept - change the club or mark the shot in Shot history.

Boxes taken out of the command centre's side drawer can always go back: drag one back onto the drawer, press its → drawer while arranging, or use Arrange ▾ to put them all back. While arranging, a box in the drawer only comes out when it's dragged out.

Recording: the YouTube and Finish layouts are new. YouTube has a neat column down the left (the hole, the player, your cameras, and the flight path while the ball flies) and lighter numbers along the bottom. Finish shows the round card with your first camera in the corner. Layouts you never changed update by themselves.
Rain: the long grass and rough far off no longer turn a pale grey after rain, which made the trees on them look as if they were standing on a fairway.
Trees no longer hang over the next hole's fairway or green: each tree is kept clear of other holes by the reach of its crown, not just its trunk.
Grass tufts no longer grow on a neighbouring hole's green or fairway.

Trees look more natural: looking towards the sun, the leaves no longer glow a bright yellow-green that bled through the crowns, and the leaves have no pale rim round them. On Ultra the leaves, and the sun's rays through them, flicker less - in recordings too, where the picture is also shrunk more smoothly.

Menu → Play → The round: Restart the round starts the same course again from the 1st tee, and End the round finishes it now - its scorecard comes up, the scores so far are kept, and the videos and the demo can play.

Command centre: the Game screen box has Game | Recording on its heading - switch it to see what's being recorded, live, right there. The small recording box no longer pops up on the game window while you arrange it (unless you've chosen it).
Command centre: the course's Options (gimmes, green speed, wind, sky and the rest) now sit in the drawer down the right with the keys and the shot history, out of the way of the other boxes.

High and Ultra: pines, Scots pines, spruces and column conifers now have close-up versions too - branches under each tier of needles, the trunk showing up through the tiers and finer, denser needles - and dead trees get twigs, broken stubs and a splintered top. On Ultra every tree on the hole you are playing is drawn this way.

Messages no longer pop up in big words on the game screen and vanish: a small speech-bubble symbol pops up instead, and the words go to a new Messages box in the command centre that always shows the last few (up to eight, newest first, with the time, in 12pt). In one window, click the symbol to see them. The demo videos and the speed test still show their own words.

Pines, spruces and the other conifers (Medium and up) no longer have a solid green cone inside them showing between the branches - they're needles all the way through now, with needles under each tier and the trunk running up through the middle.

High and Ultra: the trees lining the hole now have the same leafy look as the nearest ones - each leaf its own shade and the sun showing through - so an oak 45 m away no longer looks a flat, dark green. And spruces are fuller: no more gaps between their upper tiers.

Recording: pressing Record now asks what to record - Full screen (the game window just as it shows, its own numbers, cards and messages too) or one of your scenes. Enter takes what you recorded last. To skip the question, set What to record in the Recording panel's Recording and sound.

Recording: see what's being recorded on the game screen. Shift + Q flicks the game window to the recording and back, and the Recording panel's On the game window can show it in a small box while you record (move and size it with Shift + B, like the other boxes).

Recording: the YouTube layout is new - the game to the right, and down the left the player, the hole and your cameras, with the flight path while the ball flies and the second camera close up after it lands; the mini map and ten numbers along the bottom. A YouTube layout you never changed becomes the new one.
Recording: scenes can now be saved to a file and brought in from one (Recording, then Scenes, then Scene files), to take your scenes to another PC.

Recording: the scene designer, a web page with the Recording panel's designer on it and nothing to install. Design scenes over a game picture with sample cameras and a sample shot, save them to a file, and bring them into the game.
Recording: two ready-made scenes come with the game, Broadcast and Broadcast with camera, beside the presets.
Recording: in the layer list, a long name no longer pushes the copy and remove buttons off the side.
Recording designer: boxes lock onto each other's edges (and the picture's) from further away, with a pink line showing where they meet, so they sit together cleanly.
Recording designer: type a box's left, top, width and height in pixels; Shift + click picks several to line up, make the same size, butt together with no gaps, or group so they move together.
Recording designer: outlines can be as thick as you like, a camera's border has a thickness and colour, and a new Background box sits behind other boxes.

Course designer: Make the course now finds the best course it can. It plays every hole in the head, tries other designs of the holes that are weak - no better side to drive to, nothing round a par 3's green that anyone finds - and keeps the best, then says which holes it changed and the review's score before and after. Pick how hard it looks with Best holes, or turn it off; Stop keeps the best so far.

Golf Sim Links: trees by the 13th's pond no longer sink a metre into the grass, and a tree seen past the 17th no longer floats above the ground. On designed courses, the trees round a hole now stand on the ground as it's drawn.
Fixed: after playing shots on a hole, the next hole never loaded (hole 2 stayed on the loading card).
Ultra: every tree along the hole you are playing is now drawn at its finest the whole time, so the trees down the fairway no longer look rough or wait to improve as you play up the hole.

Ultra: the hole's flyover and the J replay are no longer blurred all over: the ball, the trees along the hole and the green ahead stay sharp, with only the grass right by the camera and the far distance softly out of focus.

Trees further off are now leafy, lighter versions of each kind (its own leaves, colour, season and sway) instead of chunky lumps. On High and Ultra none at all on the hole you are playing: the trees on the neighbouring holes nearby are real trees too.
Nine Oaks' greens now have Moderate slopes, with more to read than before. Nine Oaks Mountain has them too. The holes and pins are just as they were.

The ready-made courses are made again with today's course maker: Golf Sim Links' bunker walls are back on the bunkers by the 1st and 13th greens, and Sea Links' pot bunkers and cart paths are drawn as the game draws them now. A ready-made course you've changed is kept as your own copy.

On the courses laid out on hills, trees no longer stand on the cart paths, beside the tees or on another hole's fairway, green or tee, and the trees out past a hole stand on the ground rather than just above it. Courses on hills you've made yourself get the same as they load.
Behind the scenes: the game can be started on the newer graphics engine for testing it a piece at a time, with a tool that compares its picture with today's. Nothing should play differently.
The ball is drawn its real size wherever it sits or rolls - on the course, the range, chipping and the Challenges - and grows only in the air, so you can still follow it.
Messages on the game screen are half the size they were, and the command centre's copy of them is as small as the rest of its text.

Recording: a long recording goes on in a new file every hour with nothing missed between them, and an earlier hour is never deleted to make room for the next. A Quality choice (Best, Standard, Compact) makes smaller files.

While recording, Ultra draws the picture at the screen's own size, which is much lighter on the graphics card. If the recording's encoder fails it says why and carries on in a new file, and it stops (saying so) only if it keeps failing.
Shot screen: every shot in its history has a Replay of that shot, and the last ten can be marked (thin, fat, ignore and the rest) or put down to another club, as in the command centre.
A camera replay never plays a shot from another day that happened to have the same number.
If the Omni stays connected but stops sending anything, the game says so and connects to it again. If it keeps going quiet (asleep, say), it tells you rather than trying again and again.
Problem reports now show the graphics card's name again, memory use through the session, any graphics card reset, and why a recording stopped.
Trees: each kind has its own leaves (oak, birch, poplar, willow and the rest), and birches and willows have new crowns. On Ultra the most detailed trees reach 120 m.
Replaying the hole just finished (J) shows it straight away, instead of building it again first.
Behind the scenes: groundwork for a newer graphics engine. Nothing should play differently.

While recording, a picture that stays slow is eased between shots even with Don't adjust automatically ticked (a message says so), and put back as you chose it when you stop - a slow picture while recording could stall the graphics card.
A long recording says, as each new hourly file starts, if older recordings are about to be deleted to make room.
Problem reports show how much each view really draws, the memory at any freeze, and whether the command centre's live game picture was on.
New in the Menu: What's new - this version's changes at the top, and every version since 3.0 below it.
High graphics now has the same soft shadows as Ultra: sharp at a tree's foot, softer from its crown.
Far rough (Medium and up) is painted as standing grass past the long grass, rather than flat ground.
Behind the scenes: hole editing code tidied and the guide split into a page per subject. Nothing should play differently.
Voice: nothing pops up unless you've said the wake word, only one voice pop-up shows at a time, and a doubtful reading just gets a plain note.
From the air, the other holes on the course are drawn plainly, and the front row of trees is drawn in finer detail.
Behind the scenes: a course-wide height map (the first step towards drawing whole courses more efficiently) and faster green shaping. Nothing should play differently.

Past the hole you are playing, the ground follows the course, and nearby holes and the next hole show their greens, fairways, sand and simple trees. The hole itself looks the same, and so does the minimap.

Courses: trees never stand on another hole's fairway, green or tee, and every hole shows the same trees in the same places. The gap between two holes can still keep a narrow line of trees. In the hole editor, other holes' fairways and trees are shown in red: a tree can't be planted or moved onto another hole's fairway, green or tee, and tapping another hole's tree says 'Belongs to hole N'. Heather, gorse, rocks, flowers and bushes are no longer scattered on other holes' fairways, greens or tees either. You can now plant a tree by hand on a hole's own fairway, as long as it's at least 1 m from the line of play. A new Decor tool in the hole editor places, moves and removes heather, gorse, rocks, wildflowers and bushes. They're saved with the hole, look the same from every hole, and can go on the hole's own fairway but not on its green or tee, or on another hole's ground. Another hole's decor shows as 'Belongs to hole N'. Other holes seen from the one you're playing are now mown in their own stripes, so they look just as they do when you play them. The designer has a Fairway mowing and a Green mowing choice for each hole: Auto keeps the pattern it has now.

Around each hole, the ground is finer near play, a board at the next tee shows its number and par, the hole-change card shows par and yards, and the nearest trees look sharper on High and Ultra. Click the bay map to see the holes around this one.
New versions now come out when they're ready, rather than with every change.
Behind the scenes: the course and menu code tidied into smaller parts. Nothing should play differently.
Behind the scenes: building a hole's 3D split into its own parts. Nothing should play differently.
When nothing on screen is moving, the game rests sooner (after 1 second) and checks for changes a little more often.
Behind the scenes: course code tidied. Nothing should play differently.
Smoother frames: the long grass round the ball is grown over a smaller area (20 m on High, 32 m on Ultra).
The Solo play video's hole in one goes in again now that greens play with grain.
Fixed: recording the videos (show reel and the rest) skipped every course hole - they now wait for each hole to be built.
The code inside the installer is now scrambled, so it isn't readable source.
Only the newest releases are kept for download (10 betas and 2 stable).
Holes you've played before load faster: saved holes are reused properly now.
Every course's first hole is kept ready, so starting a round and its flyover is quicker.
Saved holes can be kept in a folder of your choice, such as another drive.
The game always opens on the driving range.
Who's playing now floats over the command centre when it opens.
Range balls can be hit as a warm-up before you press Play - nothing is recorded until then.
The speed test and demo runs build their holes before they start, with a "Getting ready" card, so there's no pause between holes.
Holes are kept on this PC once built, so a hole built again loads much faster.
